description: Findings of the independent in-session review panel (six reviewers; two further lenses failed with an API overload and were re-run in round 2). Verbatim reviewer output.

findings.area: G05-05 (with G05-03, G05-04, M-DIR-08) / MASTER G05
findings.title: DISTORTED + duplicated: 'configurable and subject to validation' broadened to all daily thresholds
findings.detail:
Source, MASTER.txt l.41-42: "Normal above -2% until +5%; defensive at -2%, reduced risk and stricter quality; proposed recovery at -1.75% and emergency halt at -3%, configurable and subject to validation." The qualifier sits inside the third semicolon clause only. Brief 08 (08_Risk_Intelligence.txt l.24) confirms the scope: "Recovery and emergency thresholds configurable."

Matrix G05-05 (requirements_matrix.yaml l.711-716) reads "Thresholds configurable and subject to validation." The word "Thresholds" is not in the source and is unqualified. The same clause is also attached as a parenthetical to G05-03 (l.695) and G05-04 (l.705), so one source clause lives under three ids.

The broad reading has already propagated:
- specifications/research_parameters.toml l.3-5: "Every number here is a PROPOSED RESEARCH PARAMETER ... and all are \"configurable and subject to validation\" (G05-05)". The file includes the -2% defensive trigger (l.29-33, G05-02) and the +5% profit-protection trigger (l.47-51, G05-06).
- CLAUDE.md rule 8 lists "-2 % / -1.75 % / -3 % / +5 %" as research parameters.

The specification labels neither -2% nor +5% as "proposed"; M-DIR-08 covers only "Proposed numerical settings". No open item records this interpretation (U-03 in docs/DECISION_LOG.md covers only the meaning of -1.75%). Sessions 08 and 10 can therefore diverge on whether the defensive and profit-protection triggers may be tuned during validation.
findings.proposed_change: Reword G05-05 to "Recovery (-1.75%) and emergency-halt (-3%) thresholds are configurable and subject to validation" and remove the duplicate parentheticals from G05-03/G05-04 (one id per clause). Add an open item for the owner: "Are -2% (defensive) and +5% (profit floor) fixed, or also research parameters?" Until it is answered, change the header of research_parameters.toml and CLAUDE.md rule 8 so they do not cite G05-05 for those two values.

findings.area: OWNER_DIRECTIVE_2026-11-27.md (first sentence) / OWN
findings.title: MISSING: first sentence of the owner directive has no requirement id
findings.detail:
OWNER_DIRECTIVE_2026-11-27.md l.7-8: "The ZIP contains the complete Gold Intelligence Engine project specification and all 13 specialist development briefs." OWN-01 (requirements_matrix.yaml l.1652-1656) starts at the second sentence. The directive has 15 sentences; the matrix has OWN-01..14.

The matrix does capture other purely informational clauses (M-AUTH-01, G01-11, G03-13) and defines status `not_applicable` for them (l.13). This sentence also defines the "complete specification" / "agreed scope" that OWN-05 refers to, and contains a checkable fact (13 briefs).
findings.proposed_change: Add OWN-15 with the verbatim sentence, sessions [S00], evidence = specifications/source/SHA256SUMS listing 13 briefs plus MASTER. Update the directive header line "OWN-01 .. OWN-14" accordingly. Do not renumber existing ids.

findings.area: M-AUTH-14
findings.title: MERGED + session list narrows a universal safety prohibition
findings.detail:
Source, MASTER.txt l.11-12: "Paper/replay only; build execution interfaces but keep real order routing disabled." M-AUTH-14 (requirements_matrix.yaml l.150-155) keeps both halves in one entry with sessions [S00, S07]. It is the only M-AUTH entry not assigned to all 13 sessions.

The sentence is part of the integrated prompt of every brief: COM-04 (l.1572), assigned to all sessions, says "text identical to MASTER 'Authority and scope' (see M-AUTH-01..18)". Brief 11 l.24 adds "No direct order route" and brief 12 "check data leakage and live lock".

The two halves are different obligations: a constructive one (S00 contracts / S07) and a prohibition on everyone. With one status, the prohibition cannot be `verified` until S07 builds the interfaces, and a per-session view hides it from 11 sessions. The rule itself is still tracked for all sessions via G08-10, M-DIR-07, OWN-14 and COM-11, so it is not unenforced.
findings.proposed_change: Keep M-AUTH-14 as "Build execution interfaces." [S00, S07] and add M-AUTH-19 "Keep real order routing disabled." with all 13 sessions.

findings.area: OWN-08
findings.title: MERGED: four persistent registers tracked under one id
findings.detail:
OWNER_DIRECTIVE l.25-26: "Maintain a persistent requirements matrix, implementation status, decision log and acceptance test register throughout development." OWN-08 (requirements_matrix.yaml l.1725-1731) keeps all four artefacts in one entry.

Elsewhere the matrix splits lists per item (S00-ASG-26/27/28 "Create CLAUDE.md." / "Create decision log." / "Create requirements matrix."). The four registers have different artefacts and different states at review time: requirements_matrix.yaml, acceptance_tests.yaml and docs/DECISION_LOG.md exist; docs/IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md (announced in the CLAUDE.md path table) does not exist yet. A single status cannot express that.
findings.proposed_change: Split into four entries (keep OWN-08 for the requirements matrix; add ids for implementation status, decision log and acceptance test register), each naming its artefact path.

findings.area: OWN-09 (also OWN-04)
findings.title: MERGED: four separate prohibitions in one id; 'omit requirements' is tracked nowhere else
findings.detail:
OWNER_DIRECTIVE l.28-29: "Do not silently simplify functionality, substitute placeholders, omit requirements or declare incomplete components finished." OWN-09 (requirements_matrix.yaml l.1736-1742) is one entry.

The equivalent MASTER sentence was atomised into M-AUTH-06/07/08 ("Never silently simplify." / "Never invent data." / "Never mark placeholders complete."). "omit requirements" has no MASTER twin, so the only place it is tracked is inside this four-part bundle.

Same pattern, lower impact: OWN-04 bundles "Treat ChatGPT as the architectural supervisor and independent reviewer" with "me as the project owner with final authority".
findings.proposed_change: Split OWN-09 into four entries (simplify functionality / substitute placeholders / omit requirements / declare incomplete components finished). Optionally split OWN-04 into two.

findings.area: OWN-11
findings.title: MERGED: 'Complete Session 00' plus four distinct submissions in one id
findings.detail:
OWNER_DIRECTIVE l.33-34: "Complete Session 00 and submit the foundation review PDF, shared contracts, source files and test evidence." OWN-11 (requirements_matrix.yaml l.1757-1762) is a single entry.

These are five checkable items: completion, review PDF, shared contracts, source files, test evidence. The matrix splits the comparable brief list into S00-DEL-01..06. /home/user/Hello/reviews/session_00/ is empty at review time, so a single status would hide which deliverable is outstanding.
findings.proposed_change: Split into: complete Session 00; submit foundation review PDF; submit shared contracts; submit source files; submit test evidence.

findings.area: OWN-01
findings.title: MERGED / MISASSIGNED: 'implement the entire project' assigned to S00 only
findings.detail:
OWNER_DIRECTIVE l.10: "You will coordinate and implement the entire project within this session." OWN-01 (requirements_matrix.yaml l.1652-1657) has sessions [S00].

The sentence holds two obligations: coordinate, and implement the entire project (the work of briefs 01-12) inside one session. D-001 in docs/DECISION_LOG.md uses it to override COM-01 for every brief. With sessions [S00], the Session 00 gate either can never close OWN-01 or closes "implement the entire project" prematurely.
findings.proposed_change: Split into "Coordinate the entire project within this session" [S00] and "Implement the entire project within this session" [S00..S12]; or keep one entry with all sessions and a note that it stays open until the last session.

findings.title: MISASSIGNED + MERGED: 'Historical replay' omits Session 01
findings.detail:
G07-01 (requirements_matrix.yaml l.882-887): "Historical replay and market memory." sessions [S09, S10, S04].

Brief 01 (01_Market_Data.txt l.22): "Implement timestamped raw bid/ask tick ingestion and storage, historical replay, candle construction..."; the matrix itself has S01-ASG-03 "Implement historical replay." S01 is missing from G07-01.

The entry also merges two items with different owners: replay (S01, S10) and market memory (S04 "historical similarity retrieval", S09).
findings.proposed_change: Split into "Historical replay" [S01, S10, S09] and "Market memory" [S04, S09]; at minimum add S01 to G07-01.

findings.area: M-DIR-05 (also M-DIR-06)
findings.title: MERGED + MISASSIGNED: early scaffolding for research and QA tracked under S00 only
findings.detail:
MASTER.txt l.80-81: "Wave 4: 09, 10, 11, 12; research and QA start scaffolding earlier." M-DIR-05 (requirements_matrix.yaml l.1412-1417) keeps both semicolon-separated clauses in one entry with sessions [S00].

The second clause instructs S10 and S12: brief 10 l.7 "begin harness early; integrated modules later"; brief 12 l.7 "ongoing through all waves". dependency_graph.yaml records it correctly (early_scaffolding: true, l.37 and l.43), so the content is not lost; only the matrix tracking is wrong.

Similar: M-DIR-06 "Coordinator alone integrates reviewed branches." (l.1422-1427) is [S00] only, although it is equally a prohibition on every other session (brief 12: "Do not ... silently fix other branches").
findings.proposed_change: Split M-DIR-05 into "Wave 4: 09, 10, 11, 12." [S00] and "Research and QA start scaffolding earlier." [S00, S10, S12]. Set M-DIR-06 sessions to all 13.

findings.area: M-AUTH-16, M-AUTH-17
findings.title: MERGED: seven record items and two deliverables in single ids
findings.detail:
MASTER.txt l.12-14: "Record exact commit, files, tests, commands, results, limitations and requirement IDs. Submit a PDF review plus machine-readable evidence;"

M-AUTH-16 (requirements_matrix.yaml l.170-175) holds all seven record items in one entry. The parallel Review-gate list is atomised into M-GATE-01..07, and brief lists are split per item (S00-ASG-02..07). "limitations" has no M-GATE counterpart, so it is tracked only inside this bundle.

M-AUTH-17 (l.180-185) bundles the PDF review and the machine-readable evidence, which are two separately checkable deliverables.
findings.proposed_change: Split M-AUTH-16 per item (commit, files, tests, commands, results, limitations, requirement IDs) and M-AUTH-17 into PDF review / machine-readable evidence.

findings.area: M-GATE-09, M-GATE-07
findings.title: MERGED: merge authorisation and model-promotion authorisation share one id
findings.detail:
MASTER.txt l.87: "Owner authorizes merge and model promotion." M-GATE-09 (requirements_matrix.yaml l.1532-1537) is one entry for all sessions.

Merge authorisation applies to every session (cf. M-AUTH-11); model promotion applies to the model-producing sessions (cf. G07-10 [S09, S00], brief 09 "require owner-approved promotion"). These are two different gates with different evidence.

M-GATE-07 "Every session delivers blockers and change requests." (l.1512) similarly joins two register items, while its siblings M-GATE-01..06 are one item each.
findings.proposed_change: Split M-GATE-09 into "Owner authorizes merge." [all] and "Owner authorizes model promotion." [S04, S09, S00]. Split M-GATE-07 into blockers / change requests.

findings.title: MERGED: nine external data sources plus a licensing condition in one id
findings.detail:
G06-06 (requirements_matrix.yaml l.841-847): "Observe XAGUSD, DXY, GC futures, Treasury yields, real yields, S&P 500, VIX, USDJPY and timestamped news where licensed and available."

Elsewhere the matrix splits lists per item (G04-02..07, G10-08..16, S00-ASG-11..19). Licensing and availability differ per source; open item U-09 in docs/DECISION_LOG.md already asks about them individually. With one id, a `partial` status cannot show which sources are observed, unlicensed or omitted, which works against OWN-09 ("omit requirements"). S03-ASG-01 carries the same bundled list.
findings.proposed_change: Split into one entry per source, each with the condition "where licensed and available"; or keep G06-06 and add a mandatory per-source status list in `contributions`.

findings.title: MISASSIGNED: two halves of one prohibition have inconsistent session lists
findings.detail:
MASTER.txt l.30: "No network LLM or training in critical path." The matrix splits this into G03-05 "No network LLM in critical path." with all 13 sessions (l.441) and G03-06 "No training in critical path." with [S04, S09, S06] only (l.451-456).

The critical path (tick -> decision -> risk -> order) is owned by S01, S05, S07 and S08 as well. CLAUDE.md code rules already state the rule universally: "No network calls, LLM calls or model training in any tick/decision path."
findings.proposed_change: Give G03-06 the same session list as G03-05 (all sessions), or at least add S01, S05, S07, S08.

findings.title: MISASSIGNED: 'Reject stale signals' omits Session 03 (and 01)
findings.detail:
G03-12 (requirements_matrix.yaml l.511-516): "Reject stale signals." sessions [S00, S05, S06, S07, S08].

Brief 03 (03_Intermarket_Intelligence.txt l.24, l.33): "handle futures rolls and stale feeds" and acceptance test "delayed-feed rejection". Brief 01 (l.23, l.32): "feed freshness" and "stale tick tests". Brief 08, which is listed, contains no staleness clause.
findings.proposed_change: Add S03 and S01 to G03-12.

findings.title: DISTORTED: trigger condition 'Above +5%' lost when the clause was split
findings.detail:
MASTER.txt l.42-44: "Above +5% protect a nondecreasing daily profit floor, exceptional setups only with surplus risk budget after costs and open exposure."

G05-07 (requirements_matrix.yaml l.731-735): "Exceptional setups only with surplus risk budget after costs and open exposure." Standing alone it reads as a general rule for exceptional setups in every daily state. The condition that makes it the rule for new risk above +5% is gone. Other split entries were given context (G05-03/04, G09-03); this one was not.
findings.proposed_change: Reword to "Above +5%: exceptional setups only with surplus risk budget after costs and open exposure."

findings.title: DISTORTED: scope of 'setup-specific' silently resolved
findings.detail:
MASTER.txt l.24-25: "Build setup-specific expected net R, uncertainty, price destinations and flexible trade plans".

Matrix: G02-04 "Build uncertainty (for setup-specific expected net R)." (l.341-345) narrows uncertainty to the net-R estimate. G02-05 "Build price destinations." and G02-06 "Build flexible trade plans." (l.351-365) drop "setup-specific".

The adjective can equally govern the whole list. Brief 04 points that way: "setup-specific interactions ... scenario destinations ... estimate uncertainty, holding time and expected costs" and "calibration by setup and session". The matrix picks one reading without a note or open item.
findings.proposed_change: Use "Build setup-specific uncertainty.", "Build setup-specific price destinations.", "Build setup-specific flexible trade plans." or keep the neutral verbatim fragment and put the interpretation in `notes` with an open item.

findings.title: DISTORTED / MERGED: 'Round 2' scope dropped, 'to be reconciled' added, four figures bundled
findings.detail:
MASTER.txt l.67-68: "Round 2: 23,481 setups; GCE-B 134 trades +0.462R, 18% day coverage, 4.9% drawdown at 0.5% risk; no corrected statistical significance." "Round 2:" heads the whole sentence.

- G09-02 (requirements_matrix.yaml l.1112-1116) and G09-03 (l.1122) no longer say the figures are Round 2 results. That matters because G02-09 separately requires "exact Round 1 baselines".
- G09-01 (l.1106) adds "to be reconciled". The source lists as reconcile items only "429 vs 473 Cavemen trades, daily breach denominators and live delay" (l.69-70).
- G09-02 bundles four separately checkable figures (134 trades; +0.462R; 18% day coverage; 4.9% drawdown at 0.5% risk). Open item U-05 already asks three separate questions about them.
findings.proposed_change: Prefix G09-02 and G09-03 with "Round 2:". Move "to be reconciled" from the G09-01 text into `notes`. Split G09-02 into four entries.

findings.title: MERGED: entries whose parts belong to different sessions or are separately testable
findings.detail:
- G05-02 "Defensive at -2%, reduced risk and stricter quality." (l.681-686): state trigger and reduced risk are S08; stricter quality is the decision/quality gate (S05).
- G01-10 "Never force trades or leverage." (l.290-295): forcing trades is S05, forcing leverage is S08.
- G04-13 "Fast monotonic profit ratchet based on executable net P&L." (l.651): three properties that brief 06 lists separately ("executable net P&L peak tracking, monotonic stops, fast giveback protection").
- G06-01 "Scheduled news and unexpected volatility mode." (l.791): the matrix itself splits the brief equivalent into S03-ASG-06 / S03-ASG-07.
- G03-04 "Strategic on completed candles and asynchronous background updates." (l.431): two cadences.
- G10-16 "Report failures and uncertainty." (l.1352): its siblings G10-08..15 are one metric each.
- G03-01 "Anticipate, prepare, react, protect." (l.401): four phases.
- M-AUTH-12 (l.130): four protected systems (Gold Bot, AI trader, breakout bot, GCE baselines).

This is inconsistent with the per-item splitting used for G04-02..07, G10-08..15 and S00-ASG-02..19.
findings.proposed_change: Split where the parts have different owners or tests (G05-02 into 3, G01-10 into 2, G04-13 into 3, G06-01 into 2, G10-16 into 2). The others may stay bundled if a note lists the sub-items to be evidenced individually.

findings.title: Coordinator glosses are mixed into requirement `text` with no documented marker
findings.detail:
Seventeen MASTER entries carry parenthetical additions that are not the owner's words, for example "(research goal)", "(into risk)", "(ratchet/dynamic protection)", "(on the account)", "(existing evidence, to be reconciled)". The matrix header (requirements_matrix.yaml l.3-5) does not say that parentheses mark coordinator context. M-AUTH-01 contains the owner's own parenthesis "(GIE)", so a reader cannot tell the two apart. The dedicated `notes` field is empty on all 524 entries.

Some glosses assert an interpretation. G04-05 "Aggregate margin (into risk)." and G04-06 "Aggregate costs (into risk)." (l.571 onward) differ from brief 08 l.22, which lists "aggregate exposure, margin, pending risk, gap stress" as parallel items; there margin is a separate account constraint, not a component of risk.
findings.proposed_change: Keep `text` verbatim from the source and move every gloss into `notes` (or a new `context` field); or state the convention in the matrix description. Reword G04-04..07 neutrally, e.g. "Aggregate limits account for margin."

findings.area: MASTER header/footer
findings.title: MISSING: document label 'Paper / research only' and version V1.0 have no id; source provenance incomplete
findings.detail:
MASTER.txt l.1 "GIE / ENGINEERING SPECIFICATION / V1.0" and the footer on both pages (l.48, l.92) "GIE | 27 Nov 2026 | Paper / research only" are not captured. The footer also appears on every brief. "Paper / research only" is not the same wording as M-AUTH-13 "Paper/replay only".

All 152 MASTER entries carry `source: MASTER.pdf` without version or hash. The directive header names "MASTER_1.pdf", while the repository holds MASTER.pdf (sha256 cc81416f...) and MASTER_owner_upload.pdf (sha256 d4ca89df...) with no statement of which is which. I confirmed both yield identical text (extracted sha256 8b6cc8fb... for both), so no requirement content is affected.
findings.proposed_change: Add one informational entry (e.g. M-DOC-01: "Specification V1.0, 27 Nov 2026, labelled 'Paper / research only' on every page"). Add a provenance line to the matrix header mapping MASTER_1.pdf to MASTER_owner_upload.pdf with both sha256 values. Point the OWN `source` at specifications/source/OWNER_DIRECTIVE_2026-11-27.md.

findings.area: OWN-08 / matrix status fields (M-AUTH, G, M-DIR, M-GATE, OWN)
findings.title: Status, notes and contributions are unpopulated for all entries at review time (work in progress)
findings.detail:
All 524 entries have status `not_started`, notes '' and contributions [].

- Informational clauses that the matrix's own vocabulary says should be `not_applicable` "justified in notes" (l.13) are not marked: M-AUTH-01, G01-11, G03-13.
- Entries with delivered Session 00 artefacts are not marked either: S00-ASG-26/27/28 (CLAUDE.md, decision log, matrix), G08-03 (gie/core/routing_lock.py).
- The matrix description (l.4-5) says specifications/REQUIREMENTS_MATRIX.md "is rendered from it by tools/gie_registers.py"; neither file exists. docs/IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md (CLAUDE.md path table) is also absent.

OWN-08 requires these registers "throughout development". The commits are marked WIP, so this is a to-do before the gate rather than a defect in the extraction.
findings.proposed_change: Before the review gate: set statuses with evidence, mark informational clauses `not_applicable` with a note, and deliver tools/gie_registers.py plus the rendered REQUIREMENTS_MATRIX.md and IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md; or remove the references and raise a change request.

findings.area: MASTER / OWN cross-references
findings.title: Beyond the spec: the same rule under several ids has no cross-reference field
findings.detail:
The id uniqueness check passed, and no source clause other than the G05 qualifier (first finding) is duplicated under two ids. Several distinct source clauses restate one rule and are correctly separate ids:
- real execution disabled: M-AUTH-14, G08-10, M-DIR-07, OWN-14, COM-11
- start with Session 00: M-DIR-01, OWN-07
- preserve existing systems: M-AUTH-12, OWN-13
- gold only: G01-01, G06-07
- staleness: G03-12, G06-04

The schema has no `related` field. A test marked with one id (for example `@pytest.mark.requirement("G08-10")`) leaves its siblings without evidence, and their session lists can drift apart, as M-AUTH-14 shows. The specification does not require such a field.
findings.proposed_change: Optional: add a `related: [ids]` field and let the register tool propagate evidence or at least warn when related ids have different status or session lists.

findings.title: DISTORTED: ambiguous list '... news and intermarket ablations' was resolved silently to one reading
findings.detail: Source, specifications/extracted/10_Research_and_Backtesting.txt:23: "Test hybrid, multiple positions, sizing, exits, news and intermarket ablations." Matrix, specifications/requirements_matrix.yaml:4537-4596: S10-ASG-04 "Test hybrid.", S10-ASG-05 "Test multiple positions.", S10-ASG-06 "Test sizing.", S10-ASG-07 "Test exits.", S10-ASG-08 "Test news ablations.", S10-ASG-09 "Test intermarket ablations." The head noun 'ablations' was attached to the last two items only. The other grammatical reading (ablation studies of all six components: hybrid, multiple positions, sizing, exits, news, intermarket) is at least as plausible and is supported elsewhere in the specification (MASTER.txt:37-38 "Compare against fixed exits"; 03 brief line 33-34 "incremental out-of-period value versus gold-only"; 10 brief deliverable "frequency-expectancy frontier"). `notes` is empty for all six entries and none of the open items U-01..U-13 in docs/DECISION_LOG.md records the choice. As written, "Test hybrid." can be satisfied by a smoke test or by an ablation study - divergent implementations.
findings.proposed_change: Keep the six ids, but put the verbatim parent sentence into each entry (notes or a new `source_clause` field), state both readings in notes, and add an open item for the owner (e.g. U-14 'Does "ablations" apply to all six items of the S10 list?'). Until answered, word S10-ASG-04..07 so that the stricter reading is not lost, e.g. "Test hybrid (ablation, see source clause)."

findings.area: requirements_matrix.yaml status/notes (S00-ASG-01..07, S00-ACC-05, S00-ACC-06, S00-DEL-04, COM-01, S12-DEP-02)
findings.title: Matrix does not reflect the recorded blocker, change requests and decisions (all 524 entries not_started, every notes/contributions field empty)
findings.detail: Measured at 10:07: Counter({'not_started': 524}); 0 entries with non-empty `notes` or `contributions` (file last written 09:30:40, before docs/ existed). But docs/CHANGE_REQUESTS.md:18 (B-001) lists S00-ASG-01..07, S00-ACC-05, S00-ACC-06, S00-DEL-04, G02-08, G02-09 as blocked; CR-001 (lines 62-70) replaces COM-01 "Open a dedicated Claude Code session and worktree"; CR-002 (lines 72-80) changes S12-DEP-02. The matrix itself defines `blocked: Cannot proceed; see the linked blocker / change request` (requirements_matrix.yaml:12), yet e.g. S00-ASG-01 (line 1817) is `status: not_started`, `notes: ''`. The header (lines 3-5) also says specifications/REQUIREMENTS_MATRIX.md is rendered by tools/gie_registers.py; neither file exists at review time. Specification: owner directive "Maintain a persistent requirements matrix, implementation status, decision log and acceptance test register throughout development" (OWN-08) and every brief's stop condition "Report failed tests and unimplemented requirements explicitly." This is a time-of-review state of work in progress; it becomes a real defect only if it reaches the review gate unchanged.
findings.proposed_change: Before the gate: set S00-ASG-01..07, S00-DEL-04, S00-ACC-05 to `blocked` with notes 'B-001' (S00-ACC-06 `partial`, B-001); add notes 'superseded by owner directive, D-001 / CR-001' to COM-01, 'CR-002 (OPEN)' to S12-DEP-02 and 'D-002 path mapping' to every S<NN>-DEP-02, 'U-03' to S08-ACC-02; fill `contributions` for what Session 00 delivered; generate REQUIREMENTS_MATRIX.md; let the register validation fail when a requirement named by an OPEN blocker is not `blocked`/`partial`.

findings.area: dependency_graph.yaml sessions vs docs/WORKTREES.md vs MASTER Implementation directive
findings.title: Meaning of depends_on / contract_only differs between graph and worktree instructions; the literal worktree rule takes 07 out of Wave 2
findings.detail: specifications/dependency_graph.yaml:9: "depends_on - the dependency's review package must be approved before integration". docs/WORKTREES.md:16-17: "A session branch is created from the development branch **after** the owner has approved everything the session depends on (`specifications/dependency_graph.yaml`)." Graph line 22: S07 is wave 2 with depends_on [S00, S01]; MASTER.txt:79 says "Wave 2: 01, 02, 07, 08." Under the WORKTREES rule S07 may not even be branched until S01's review package is approved, i.e. it no longer runs in Wave 2 beside 01. If 'everything the session depends on' also covers contract_only, S07 (contract_only [S08], line 22) and S08 (contract_only [S01, S07], line 24) wait for each other. The briefs gate integration, not start: "If a dependency is unavailable, use explicitly labeled test fixtures only; do not claim integration complete." In addition graph line 10 says contract_only contracts are "(already in 00)", while docs/CHANGE_REQUESTS.md:82-96 (CR-003) states that the data/execution contracts (Candle, BrokerCalendar, InstrumentSpec, AccountSnapshot) are not in Session 00.
findings.proposed_change: Define two gates in the graph header and use the same words in WORKTREES.md rule 1: start gate = Session 00 contracts approved and the session's wave opened by the owner (unavailable dependencies replaced by labelled fixtures, COM-07); integration gate = all depends_on review packages approved; contract_only never gates start. Change "(already in 00)" to "(in 00, plus the additional shared types of CR-003)".

findings.area: S12-DEP-02 / dependency_graph.yaml S12 owns

findings.detail: All 91 entries carry the same template `verification: pytest tests marked @pytest.mark.acceptance(...)` with status values planned/passing/failing/blocked/partial. findings.area: Tick / external data for 03 (S01-ASG-12, S03-ASG-01 and 10..17, S03-ACC-01/02, G06-06 and 10..17)
findings.title: Tick cannot carry most external feeds 03 needs; no contract exists for single-valued series, revised releases or news
findings.detail: Spec: 01 'Provide synchronized external feeds to 03'; 03 'Synchronize XAGUSD, DXY, GC, yields, real yields, S&P, VIX, USDJPY and news when available' with acceptance 'No future data or revised release leakage'. The contract set gives 01->03 only Tick (SHARED_CONTRACTS.md section 1 table l.26; section 2 l.81-82: 'Tick and Evidence may describe other observed instruments (G06-06)'). Tick requires bid and ask, both price > 0 (gie/contracts/tick.py:72-73; common.py:243 PRICE = Dec(gt='0')). Verified: Tick(bid=-0.35, ask=-0.35) and bid=0 raise GIE.CONTRACT.INVALID, so a real yield <= 0 is unrepresentable. An index, yield or VIX value has no bid/ask and would have to be copied into both fields, which is not 'exactly as observed'. Futures trades (last, volume, contract month, roll) have no fields. News items and scheduled releases (scheduled time, actual release time, first print versus revised value) have no contract at all, so S03-ACC-02 cannot be tested against any shared type. CR-003 (docs/CHANGE_REQUESTS.md l.82-96) lists Candle, BrokerCalendar, InstrumentSpec and AccountSnapshot, nothing for external series or news.
findings.proposed_change: REQUIRED before 01 implements S01-ASG-12 and before 03 starts; add by change request: (a) Observation: series id, source, origin, seq, value (exact decimal, any sign), unit, event_time_ns (observation or period instant), publish_time_ns (nullable), receive_time_ns, vintage/revision index with a supersedes link, flags; (b) NewsEvent/CalendarEvent: event id, category, impact, currency, scheduled_time_ns, release_time_ns, receive_time_ns, actual/forecast/previous with revision index; (c) futures contract metadata (contract month, expiry/roll instant) or a roll-event record; (d) an ObservationSink interface and stream ranks next to TICK. Correct sections 1 and 2 so they no longer claim Tick covers these feeds; keep Tick for genuine two-sided quotes (XAGUSD, USDJPY, CFDs).

findings.area: Candle and broker calendar (S02-DEP-01, S01-ASG-04/05, S01-ACC-05/06/07, G03-04); dependency_graph.yaml; docs/WORKTREES.md
findings.title: Candle and broker-calendar contracts are REQUIRED before 02 can start, but the gate rules say 02 needs nothing beyond Session 00
findings.detail: Brief 02: 'Dependencies: 00; data contracts from 01'. Brief 01: 'candle construction, broker calendar'. G03: 'Strategic on completed candles'. The only market-data interface is TickSink.on_tick (gie/contracts/interfaces.py:29-32). There is no Candle contract and no calendar interface; MarketSession is an enum whose 'Boundaries are defined by the broker calendar (session 01)' (common.py:131-137) with no way for 02/03/04 to query it, yet Candidate.session requires it. 02 may not import gie.market_data (dependency_graph.yaml l.78, D-006) and may not define a shared type locally (SHARED_CONTRACTS.md l.44-47). CR-003 admits the gap ('the coordinator adds them ... before the dependent work starts'), but the gates contradict it: dependency_graph.yaml l.10 'contract_only - only the shared contracts of that session are needed (already in 00)' with S02 contract_only [S01] (l.20), and docs/WORKTREES.md l.19-21 'Sessions of the same wave start together ... contract_only dependencies never delay a start'. Adding Candle also needs S00-owned code: ordering_key/stream_name raise UnknownContractError for unregistered types (gie/contracts/ordering.py:37-39, 58-60) and StreamRank has no slot for candles (gie/core/ordering.py:42-54). Blocks the start of 02, not the approval of the nine contracts.
findings.proposed_change: Define Candle and the calendar interface in Session 00, or add a wave-2a gate (01 proposes, coordinator integrates, then 02 starts); correct dependency_graph.yaml l.10 and WORKTREES rule 1. Candle must fix at least: price basis (bid/ask/mid; PriceBasis.CANDLE_CLOSE depends on it); explicit open_time_ns/close_time_ns (broker-server bar alignment is not a function of UTC across DST, S01-ACC-05); the completion/availability instant and what triggers it (tick or timer); the revision rule for late ticks; tick count and quality flags; first/last tick seq; stream candle/<source>/<symbol>/<timeframe>; a StreamRank after TICK and before EVIDENCE; a CandleSink. Calendar interface: is_open(t), session(t) allowing overlapping sessions, next close/rollover/weekend instants, holiday-table version.

findings.area: Clock contract (gie/core/clock.py, SHARED_CONTRACTS 3.2); S01-ASG-08, S01-ACC-04, G08-06, G03-03/04, S02-ACC-05, S03-ASG-06
findings.title: No timer or heartbeat interface: everything that must happen when no tick arrives is left to each session
findings.detail: The Clock Protocol exposes only mode, now_ns and monotonic_ns (gie/core/clock.py:40-54). Timers exist only as ReplayClock.call_at (l.106); SystemClock has none (verified). ClockReading is 'used for heartbeats', but no producer, cadence or sink is defined (only TickSink and RecordSink exist). Specified behaviour that occurs without a tick: feed freshness and stale-tick tests (a silent feed produces no on_tick; G08-06 'Disconnect/stale-feed fail closed'); closing a candle at its boundary in a quiet market (G03-04), which also bounds S02-ACC-05; emitting EXPIRED evidence; 'Tactical every tick or second' (G03-03); scheduled-news windows. Each session would use its own thread timer in paper and something else in replay, so paper/replay equivalence and the byte-identical replay of section 6.2 (l.239-241) are not guaranteed.
findings.proposed_change: Add a Scheduler Protocol (call_at(due_ns, callback) -> handle, cancel(handle)) to the Clock contract, implemented by ReplayClock (already present) and by a paper-mode implementation in gie.core, injected together with the Clock. State normatively that timers due at t fire before any tick with receive_time_ns == t (this matches advance_to and StreamRank.CLOCK = 0) and that callbacks run on the dispatch thread. Alternative: an on_clock(ClockReading) heartbeat sink with a research-parameter cadence.

findings.area: Freshness (SHARED_CONTRACTS 3.3, gie/core/freshness.py, TickFlag.STALE); S01-ACC-04, S03-ACC-03, S03-ASG-05
findings.title: The reference instant of tick freshness is undefined and conflicts with EVENT_AFTER_RECEIVE; STALE does not mean 'feed silent'
findings.detail: Section 3.3 l.129: 'Data with a reference instant is fresh iff 0 <= now_ns - reference_ns < max_age_ns'; which Tick time is the reference is not stated. TickFlag.STALE is 'Received later after its source timestamp than the feed-freshness limit' (tick.py:33-34), i.e. transport delay including broker clock offset, not time since the last tick, and no invariant enforces it. Tick legitimately allows event_time_ns > receive_time_ns (TICK-2, tick.py:102), but freshness.age_ns raises FutureDataError for any future reference (freshness.py:40-41) and l.132-133 says the tolerance 'MUST be 0 in replay'. Verified: for a valid EVENT_AFTER_RECEIVE tick, is_fresh(now=receive_time, reference=event_time) raises GIE.TIME.FUTURE; for a feed delayed 15 minutes, reference=receive_time gives fresh and reference=event_time gives stale. So S01-ACC-04, S03-ACC-03 and the stale checks of 06/07 will use different references, and a recorded paper tick from a broker clock ahead of local time would raise only in replay. research_parameters.toml has no max_age_ns for any feed although l.130 says these limits are research parameters.
findings.proposed_change: Define two quantities in section 3.3: (1) feed-silence age = now_ns minus receive_time_ns of the newest accepted tick of the stream (reference is always receive time, never in the future); this is the consumer-side test. (2) source delay = receive_time_ns - event_time_ns - estimated source clock offset, evaluated by 01 at ingest and expressed by STALE (better renamed DELAYED); this is the delayed-feed test. State that event_time_ns is never passed as reference_ns with tolerance 0. Add a helper tick_age_ns(tick, now_ns) to gie.contracts and per-source parameters max_silence_ns and max_source_delay_ns.

findings.area: Evidence.market_event_id / identity.market_event_id (S02-ASG-03, S02-ACC-02, G02-02)
findings.title: The identity parts of a market event are undefined per kind, not verified by the record, and not required to stay constant across revisions
findings.detail: Section 4 l.168-171: market_event_id(kind, symbol, timeframe, anchor_time_ns, level_prices) 'is shared by every producer that observes the same event'. Not defined: (a) which of Evidence.levels are identity levels; (b) what anchor_time_ns is ('Source event time of the market structure that defines the event', evidence.py:157-160: bar open, bar close, or the sweeping tick); (c) whether the timeframe is identity when two engines see the same sweep on M5 and M15; (d) that the id is constant over revisions, although EVD-1 makes evidence_id = f(engine, market_event_id, revision) (evidence.py:208-212), so a level that changes between FORMING and CONFIRMED breaks the chain. No invariant ties market_event_id to the record's own fields; verified: an XAUUSD/M5 Evidence accepts an id computed for ('zzz','EURUSD','D1',1,[]). The only example (tests/gie/samples.py:167-174) hashes all levels. Verified: one extra level (e.g. PENDING_LIMIT) gives a different id, M5 versus M15 gives a different id, anchor at bar open versus bar close gives a different id. Two careful implementers will not obtain equal ids, and 'exact event deduplication' can pass inside 02 while 03/04/09 producers use another convention.
findings.proposed_change: Add to section 4 a normative identity table for the three SHARED_EVIDENCE_KINDS: identity level roles (e.g. liquidity_sweep: SWEPT_LEVEL; fair_value_gap: FVG_HIGH and FVG_LOW; breakout: BREAKOUT_LEVEL), one anchor convention (e.g. open time of the defining candle as stamped by the Candle contract), and whether timeframe is identity. Require identity parts to be fixed at revision 0. Make it checkable: add identity: bool to PriceLevel (or a role registry) and invariant EVD-11: market_event_id == identity.market_event_id(kind, symbol, timeframe, anchor_time_ns, prices of identity levels).

findings.area: Evidence states INACTIVE/MISSING, NamedValue (S02-ACC-03, S02-ASG-08, S03-ACC-04)
findings.title: Inactive versus missing is defined only inside one record: no evaluation-slot rule, non-event records collide across engines, a single feature cannot be missing
findings.detail: EVD-2/EVD-5 separate the two states in a record, but: (a) nothing says when a producer must emit INACTIVE or MISSING, or for which unit (engine, or engine x kind x timeframe), so the absence of a record at time t is ambiguous for 04/05 (inactive, missing or expired). (b) INACTIVE/MISSING records still need market_event_id, kind, timeframe and anchor_time_ns although no market event exists. Verified: engine A INACTIVE and engine B MISSING for (liquidity_sweep, XAUUSD, M5, same anchor, no levels) get the same market_event_id, and section 4 says equal ids 'MUST be counted once', which would merge a known no with an unknown. (c) NamedValue.value is a required finite float (common.py:183-187) although section 5 rule 3 (l.189) says 'Unavailable data is represented as null / MISSING ... Consumers MUST NOT substitute a neutral value'; omission is the only option and no rule says omission means missing rather than 0. This is the feature-level case of 'missing-source degradation' in 03.
findings.proposed_change: Define an evaluation slot (engine, kind, symbol, timeframe) declared in the feature dictionary. Rule: after each evaluation a producer has exactly one current record per slot; a consumer treats 'no unexpired current record for a declared slot' as MISSING. Give non-event records an engine-scoped identity (e.g. identity.slot_event_id(engine, kind, symbol, timeframe, evaluation_anchor)) and exclude INACTIVE/MISSING from cross-engine de-duplication. Make NamedValue.value nullable (or add missing_features: list[code]) and state 'absent or null feature = unknown, never 0'.

findings.area: S02-ACC-05 'No five-minute notification delay'; G09-09; Evidence.anchor_time_ns / as_of_time_ns / decision_time_ns; SHARED_CONTRACTS 3.1
findings.title: The notification delay cannot be measured from contract fields, and it is zero by construction in replay
findings.detail: The contract offers anchor_time_ns (source event time, convention undefined), as_of_time_ns ('Receive time of the newest input the record depends on', common.py:224-228) and decision_time_ns; section 3.1 l.101 defines 'End-to-end delay of a decision is decision_time_ns - as_of_time_ns on the run clock'. (a) In REPLAY that difference is always 0, because ReplayClock.now_ns only changes inside advance_to (gie/core/clock.py:100-101, 144-166; verified), so an acceptance test run in replay cannot fail on it. (b) An adapter that reports a breakout one M5 bar late and stamps as_of with the input that triggered its evaluation looks identical to a timely one. (c) 'Receive time' exists only for Tick and OrderEvent; for evidence built from candles it is undefined whether as_of is the candle's availability or the underlying tick watermark. (d) No research parameter states a bound. What the existing five-minute delay is cannot be checked (B-001), but the quantity to test must exist in the contract.
findings.proposed_change: Add Evidence.observable_time_ns: availability instant of the input that first made this revision's state/stage true (e.g. the tick or timer that closed the breakout candle), with invariant observable_time_ns <= as_of_time_ns <= decision_time_ns. Define notification delay = decision_time_ns - observable_time_ns. Define the replay form of S02-ACC-05: the revision is emitted in the same processing step as the input whose availability equals observable_time_ns. Define as_of for derived inputs as the maximum of the inputs' own watermarks. Add a research parameter for the paper-mode bound.

findings.area: De-duplication (S02-ASG-10, S02-ACC-02, G02-02); SHARED_CONTRACTS section 4; Candidate.evidence_ids
findings.title: 'Counted once downstream' is undefined: no representative, no score rule, and the work the brief gives to 02 is moved to every consumer
findings.detail: Brief 02: 'Deduplicate shared sweep/FVG/breakout evidence'. Contract: 'Two Evidence records with equal market_event_id are the same market event seen by different engines and MUST be counted once downstream' (section 4 l.169-171); Candidate.evidence_ids are 'already de-duplicated by market event' (candidate.py:114). So 02 only tags; 04, 05, 09 and 11 each de-duplicate, with no rule for which record represents the event or how per-engine scores (engine A bullish 0.7, engine B 0.4) combine. No producer class is designated for an engine-neutral shared-event record (a STRATEGY_ENGINE record must name one of the six engines, EVD-9). Consumers will choose differently (first seen, highest score, lowest engine id), giving different candidates and contributions for the same inputs.
findings.proposed_change: Choose one model and write it down. (A) 02 emits one engine-neutral record per shared event (a new ProducerClass, exempt from EVD-9) and per-engine interpretation records refer to it through a new related_market_event_id. Or (B) keep per-engine records and put one pure function in gie.contracts, e.g. dedupe_by_market_event(records) -> groups, with a deterministic representative (lowest ordering_key) and the rule that scores are never summed within a group. Make S02-ACC-02 test that function.

findings.area: Evidence invariants EVD-4 / EVD-10 (G03-01, S02-ASG-06, S03-ASG-06/07, G06-01, G06-18)
findings.title: EVD-4 forbids non-directional observations: a forming range or a volatility/news regime cannot be ACTIVE
findings.detail: EVD-4: 'when state is ACTIVE at least one score is greater than 0' (evidence.py:227-231). EVD-10: 'stage is NONE when state is INACTIVE or MISSING' (l.260-267). Verified: an opening-range observation with stage FORMING and scores 0/0 is rejected by EVD-4; the same as INACTIVE with stage FORMING is rejected by EVD-10; a VOLATILITY-class 'scheduled_news' record with scores 0/0 is rejected by EVD-4. Yet G03-01 requires 'Anticipate, prepare' (stages ANTICIPATED/FORMING/ARMED exist), an opening range or consolidation has no direction before the breakout, and 03 must 'Detect scheduled and unscheduled volatility' (ProducerClass.VOLATILITY exists), which is not a bullish or bearish fact. Producers would have to invent a direction (0.5/0.5 or an epsilon), against 'never ... invent data'.
findings.proposed_change: Remove EVD-4, or narrow it to STRATEGY_ENGINE records with stage TRIGGERED or later, and document that ACTIVE with 0/0 means 'condition present, no directional information'. If a non-directional magnitude is needed (volatility intensity), add an optional intensity_score instead of overloading the directional scores.

findings.area: News restrictions and volatility mode (S03-ASG-09, G06-05, G06-01, G06-18); interfaces.py; dependency_graph.yaml
findings.title: A news restriction or volatility regime has no carrier and no path from 03 to decision and risk
findings.detail: G06-05 'Verify account news restrictions' is assigned to [S08, S03] in the matrix; brief 03: 'respect news restrictions'. 03 is listed as a producer of Evidence only (SHARED_CONTRACTS.md l.27). A restriction window is a gate, not directional evidence, and EVD-4 blocks even a neutral record. interfaces.py offers TickSink, RecordSink, RiskGate, ExecutionAdapter and ModelRegistry, none of which carries it. The dependency graph gives neither 05 (depends_on [S00, S02, S04], l.30) nor 08 (depends_on [S00], l.24) access to 03's output; only 04 lists 03 as optional (l.28). As implementer of 03 I can compute a blackout window but nothing can respect it, and fail-closed behaviour when the calendar is missing or stale is undefined.
findings.proposed_change: Add a shared MarketCondition (or TradingRestriction) contract: kind (NEWS_RESTRICTION, SCHEDULED_EVENT_WINDOW, UNSCHEDULED_VOLATILITY), source event id, start_time_ns, end_time_ns, a state that includes MISSING (calendar unavailable means no new risk), valid_until_ns. Produced by 03, consumed by 05 and 08 (surfaced as RiskDecision reason codes). Add the 03 -> 05/08 edge to dependency_graph.yaml and state which session owns the account rule (U-04) and which the calendar.

findings.area: Tick.receive_time_ns for imported history (tick.py:66-70, FIELDS l.324); S01-ACC-01, S01-ACC-08, S03-ASG-03, G09-10
findings.title: The rule for modelled receive time conflicts with stream ordering, and modelled cannot be told from measured
findings.detail: FIELDS l.324: 'For imported history without a recorded receive time it equals event_time_ns plus the modelled feed delay'. (a) Section 6.1 l.224 says 'Within a stream the ordering time MUST be non-decreasing' and merge_ordered refuses a non-ascending input (verified: GIE.SEQ.OUT_OF_ORDER). A history file with out-of-order source timestamps, the S01-ACC-01 case, then yields decreasing receive times; both rules cannot hold. (b) origin = HISTORICAL covers both a measured and a modelled availability instant, although 03 must estimate lead/lag 'using actual availability timestamps' and G09 says 'Use actual tick data for fast execution claims'. (c) The delay model is not a defined research parameter; if it is random it must be seeded and part of the run configuration for deterministic replay.
findings.proposed_change: Change the rule to receive_time_ns = max(receive_time_ns of the previous tick of the stream, event_time_ns + delay(source)) with a deterministic per-source delay parameter. Add TickFlag RECEIVE_TIME_MODELLED or a field receive_time_basis {MEASURED, MODELLED}. Require results derived from MODELLED streams to be labelled, and forbid lead/lag or latency claims finer than the modelled delay on them.

findings.area: Interfaces (gie/contracts/interfaces.py, SHARED_CONTRACTS section 10); S01-ASG-03, S01-ACC-08, G03-02/04
findings.title: Market data is push-only: no history or source interface, no owner of the replay loop, no dispatch rules
findings.detail: Only TickSink.on_tick(tick) -> None exists (interfaces.py:29-32). Missing: (a) a query side (ticks or candles for a stream and time range, latest N candles). It is needed for engine warm-up at paper start (otherwise every engine is MISSING until enough bars accumulate), for 03's lead/lag windows, and for 10, which must 'Build chronological tick replay using same decision/risk/execution interfaces as paper' but depends only on S00 (dependency_graph.yaml l.36) and cannot import 01's 'historical replay'. Who owns the loop 'advance ReplayClock, fire timers, deliver tick' is written nowhere. (b) Dispatch: 'All calls are synchronous' (interfaces.py:8; section 10 l.339), while G03 requires 'Reflex every tick' and 'Strategic on completed candles and asynchronous background updates' and ARCHITECTURE section 2 says a slow strategic task 'can never delay a protective decision'. The order of sinks, whether strategic sinks are decoupled by a queue, and what happens to the other sinks when one raises (section 5 rule 5: errors are never swallowed) are open.
findings.proposed_change: Add to gie.contracts.interfaces a MarketDataSource implemented by 01: iter_ticks(streams, start_ns, end_ns) in EventKey order, and candles(symbol, timeframe, end_ns, count). Describe the replay step normatively and name the owner (suggestion: 01 provides the ordered source, 10 the driver). Specify dispatch order (protective sinks first), per-sink exception isolation with fail-closed marking, and that strategic consumers are fed through a bounded queue in paper and in the same step in replay.

findings.area: Event ordering (SHARED_CONTRACTS 6.2, gie/core/ordering.py StreamRank, gie/contracts/ordering.py)
findings.title: Equal availability times are the normal case in replay, and the rank tie-break is not a causal order
findings.detail: Section 6.2 l.226-236: all records are processed in ascending (time_ns, rank, stream, seq); 'Execution facts therefore precede intelligence derived at the same instant'. In REPLAY every record produced while handling a tick has decision_time_ns equal to that tick's receive time, because the virtual clock does not move during processing (verified); in paper a polled feed delivers batches with one receive time. Verified sort at one instant: tick #100, tick #101, order_event, risk_decision, evidence, trade_plan. So tick #101 of the same batch precedes the evidence computed from tick #100, and a risk decision or order event precedes the plan that caused it. A journal re-read in EventKey order (09, 10, 11) does not reproduce what producers and consumers actually saw, and paper and replay interleave differently. For 02/03: a candle, a CONTRA target or a condition record at the same instant can sort after the output that used it.
findings.proposed_change: Limit EventKey ordering to exogenous inputs (ticks, observations, timers) and define the order of derived records as publication order (a run-global journal sequence assigned by the RecordSink). Or require strictly increasing logical time per causal hop (CAUSAL-1 with '<' and a minimum modelled step of 1 ns per stage in replay). State which order the 'byte for byte' replay requirement refers to.

findings.area: TickFlag consumer semantics; SequenceTracker policy for tick streams (S01-ACC-03, S01-ASG-06, G08-06)
findings.title: No rule says what a consumer must do with a flagged tick or a sequence gap
findings.detail: 'A flag never removes a tick; it tells consumers what is wrong' (tick.py:18). Nothing defines which flags exclude a tick from candle construction, evidence, simulated fills, position marking or entry decisions. 01 (candles), 02/03 (evidence), 06 and 07 will filter differently, e.g. the simulated broker fills a limit on an OUTLIER or CROSSED tick that the strategy ignored; baseline parity and deterministic replay then rest on private choices. 'Missing' has two unrelated mechanisms: GAP_BEFORE (the source lost data, heuristic) and a seq gap (GIE lost a record). Section 6.1 l.219-221 says a gap is an error 'or accepted and reported where gaps are tolerated' without saying which applies to ticks. With the default allow_gaps=False (gie/core/ordering.py:147) one lost record blocks the stream for good; verified: after 0, 1 the arrivals 3, 4, 5 are all refused with GIE.SEQ.GAP because 'A refused arrival never changes state'. For a protective consumer that is worse than the gap.
findings.proposed_change: Add a normative table to section 6.3: per TickFlag, whether the tick may be used for (a) candle/indicator input, (b) creating or increasing risk, (c) protective decisions and marking, (d) simulated fills. Implement it once in gie.contracts (e.g. tick_usable(tick, purpose)). State that Tick consumers run SequenceTracker with allow_gaps=True and treat ACCEPTED_AFTER_GAP like GAP_BEFORE (no new risk until fresh data), while OrderEvent streams stay gap-free.

findings.area: S02-ASG-09 'Expose Cavemen pending limit at breakout close'; evidence.py PENDING_LIMIT_KIND / PENDING_LIMIT_ROLE
findings.title: The pending limit is supported only by two string constants
findings.detail: The whole support is PENDING_LIMIT_KIND = 'pending_limit' and PENDING_LIMIT_ROLE = 'PENDING_LIMIT' (evidence.py:46-50) plus a role example in FIELDS (PriceLevel, l.451). Unspecified: the side of the limit (only implied by which score is > 0); the link to the breakout whose close defines it (Evidence has only supersedes_ and contradicts_ links, and adding the limit as an extra level on the breakout record changes its market_event_id); the anchor (close of the breakout candle); the order lifetime; how touched, filled and cancelled map to stage and state. No invariant exists: a kind = pending_limit record without a PENDING_LIMIT level is valid. 02 as producer and 04/05, who turn it into an EntryStyle.LIMIT plan, will diverge.
findings.proposed_change: Add a normative paragraph and invariant EVD-12: kind == pending_limit implies exactly one level with role PENDING_LIMIT and exactly one score > 0 (bullish = buy limit); related_market_event_id (new optional field) = the breakout's market_event_id; anchor_time_ns = close instant of the breakout candle; valid_until_ns = the engine's order expiry; stage ARMED while resting, TRIGGERED when reached on the executable side (ask for a buy, bid for a sell); state EXPIRED or INVALIDATED otherwise.

findings.area: EvidenceState.CONTRA, EVD-6, contradicts_evidence_id (S02-ASG-08; 05 'contradiction tests')
findings.title: CONTRA has no definition and points at one revision-specific evidence id
findings.detail: Brief 02: 'missing/contra states'. The EvidenceState docstring explains only INACTIVE versus MISSING (evidence.py:62-75); FIELDS says only 'Evidence that this record contradicts; set if and only if state is CONTRA'. EVD-6 forces exactly one contradicts_evidence_id iff CONTRA (verified in both directions). That id contains the revision (EVD-1), so the pointer is stale as soon as the contradicted observation is revised. An observation that contradicts several others, or a direction in general (a trend filter against any long), cannot be CONTRA. What the scores of a CONTRA record mean is not stated. A CONTRA record can also sort before its target at equal decision time (stream-name tie-break).
findings.proposed_change: Define CONTRA in the enum documentation, e.g. 'the producer's condition holds in the direction opposite to the referenced observation; the scores give the direction and strength of the contradicting observation'. Reference the stable chain instead of a revision: contradicts_market_event_id (plus optional engine), or allow a list. State that direction-level disagreement is expressed as ACTIVE with the opposite score.

findings.area: Evidence.bullish_score / bearish_score with symbol != XAUUSD (S03 lead/lag output, G06-07, G06-09)
findings.title: It is not stated whether scores of an intermarket record refer to the observed instrument or to gold
findings.detail: bullish_score: 'Strength of bullish evidence' (evidence.py:164-168); symbol: 'Instrument the observation is about' (l.155); section 2 l.80-82 allows Evidence about other instruments. For an INTERMARKET record with symbol = DXY or a yield series, 'bullish' can mean bullish for that instrument or for XAUUSD, the only tradable symbol. 03 and 04 can each be self-consistent and still disagree in sign. G06-09 'Never assume fixed correlations' makes the conversion a modelling step that must belong to one named party.
findings.proposed_change: State in FIELDS and section 2: bullish_score and bearish_score always express the expected direction of XAUUSD; symbol names the observed instrument; the observed instrument's own move goes into features. Add an INTERMARKET sample record to the fixtures.

findings.area: TickFlag.OUT_OF_ORDER / DUPLICATE definitions (tick.py:27-30, SHARED_CONTRACTS 6.3); S01-ACC-01/02
findings.title: OUT_OF_ORDER and DUPLICATE compare only with the immediately preceding tick, so a re-delivered block passes as clean data
findings.detail: tick.py:27-30: OUT_OF_ORDER = 'Source timestamp is earlier than that of the previous tick of the stream'; DUPLICATE = 'Same source timestamp and prices as the previous tick of the stream' (section 6.3 l.245-248: 'older than its predecessor's'). After a reconnect a feed commonly re-delivers a block: event times 100, 101, 102, 103, then again 101, 102, 103, 104. Under these definitions only the first re-delivered tick is OUT_OF_ORDER (101 < 103); 102 and 103 are neither OUT_OF_ORDER (newer than their predecessor) nor DUPLICATE (their predecessor differs) and enter candles and VWAP twice (ORB + VWAP and VWAP Trend Rider are volume-weighted by name). DUPLICATE also ignores sizes, so two genuine quotes in the same millisecond that differ only in volume are flagged. Section 11 leaves 'thresholds and detection' to 01, but these sentences are the published meaning the acceptance tests will be written against.
findings.proposed_change: Redefine: OUT_OF_ORDER = event_time_ns lower than the highest event_time_ns of any earlier tick of the stream (high-water mark); DUPLICATE = all source fields (event_time_ns, bid, ask, bid_volume, ask_volume) equal to a tick already ingested within a bounded look-back owned by 01. Or remove the 'previous tick' wording and state that the precise definitions are owned by 01 and published in its schema deliverable.

findings.area: Tick identity (source, symbol, seq) and stored history (S01-ASG-02/09/10, S01-ACC-08)
findings.title: Restart, backfill, re-import and re-flagging of stored ticks have no convention
findings.detail: 'a tick is identified by (source, symbol, seq)' (section 4 l.176); seq is 'assigned at ingest in arrival order' and 'Ticks are never modified after ingest' (tick.py:44-48). Not covered: whether seq continues across process restarts; back-filling an earlier period found by 'Audit missing history' into an existing stream; re-importing vendor history with a corrected time-zone offset; re-flagging after a change of thresholds or of the holiday table. STALE, OUTLIER and OFF_SESSION depend on tunable parameters and the calendar but are frozen inside the 'raw' record with no reference to the version that produced them.
findings.proposed_change: Specify: seq is persistent per (source, symbol). Any backfill, re-import or re-flag creates a new versioned source id (e.g. <vendor>.<dataset>.v<n>) entered in a source registry with licence status (S01-ASG-10), timestamp semantics, delay class and the hash of the quality parameters. The run configuration hash includes the source ids used.

findings.area: Timeframe enum (common.py:112-121); Evidence.timeframe / anchor_time_ns; SHARED_CONTRACTS section 11
findings.title: Timeframe is a closed, non-provisional enum and is mandatory on every Evidence
findings.detail: Timeframe = TICK, S1, M1, M5, M15, M30, H1, H4, D1. It is not in the provisional list of section 11 (l.348-350), although the engines' timeframes are unknown (B-001) and unknown enum values are refused. timeframe and anchor_time_ns are required on every Evidence, including records with no candle timeframe (lead/lag 'at seconds/minutes/hours', news events, MISSING records).
findings.proposed_change: Add Timeframe to section 11; allow null or a NONE member for evidence that is not tied to a candle; confirm the set after the audit.

findings.area: PriceLevel, Invalidation, PriceTrigger, Evidence lifecycle (S02-ASG-05/07, S02-ACC-04)
findings.title: Small gaps in levels, invalidation and the evidence lifecycle
findings.detail: (a) The unit text is 'USD per troy ounce' for any symbol (evidence.py:99, 107) and price > 0 excludes a level on a yield or spread series (verified). (b) levels has neither uniqueness nor a canonical order (evidence.py:174-176) although section 7 says lists whose order carries no meaning have a defined canonical order, so record bytes depend on emission order. (c) PriceTrigger has only AT_OR_BELOW / AT_OR_ABOVE (common.py:155-157); an engine using a strict comparison can only be mirrored with a one-tick offset, which needs the tick size (U-10) and matters for baseline parity at exact touches. (d) Basis CANDLE_CLOSE does not say which price series the candle uses. (e) It is not stated who applies an invalidation: the producer by emitting INVALIDATED, or consumers per tick. (f) There is no evidence transition rule: may an INVALIDATED or EXPIRED observation return to ACTIVE in a later revision, may a stage go backwards.
findings.proposed_change: Use 'quote currency per unit' as the unit; sort levels canonically by (role, price) and make them unique; add strict BELOW / ABOVE triggers; bind CANDLE_CLOSE to the Candle contract's price basis; add one sentence on who evaluates invalidation; add a validate_evidence_transition table in the style of the order, position and model validators.

findings.area: Research parameters (specifications/research_parameters.toml, gie/core/params.py, CLAUDE.md rule 8)
findings.title: No freshness, quality or evidence parameters exist, and sessions have no way to add them
findings.detail: Section 3.3 l.130: 'The limits (max_age_ns per feed and per decision stage) are research parameters'; CLAUDE.md rule 8: 'never hard-code them'. research_parameters.toml defines nine parameters (three latency targets, four daily thresholds, two goals); none for feed silence, source delay, modelled feed delay, outlier bounds, evidence validity or notification delay. The file lies under specifications/, owned by S00 (dependency_graph.yaml l.15), and gie.core.params loads exactly that file, so every parameter 01-03 need is a coordinator change.
findings.proposed_change: Allow per-session parameter files (e.g. specifications/research_parameters/sNN_<name>.toml, merged by the loader with the same label and validation), or define a light change-request path. Seed the file with the freshness parameters that section 3.3 refers to.

findings.area: gie/core/clock.py SystemClock (S01-ASG-11, S01-ACC-10, G03-11); pyproject.toml; .github/workflows/gie-ci.yml
findings.title: On Windows with Python below 3.13 the paper clock has about 15.6 ms granularity
findings.detail: SystemClock defaults to time.time_ns and time.monotonic_ns (clock.py:188-189). On Windows both have a documented 15.6 ms resolution before Python 3.13, which switched to GetSystemTimePreciseAsFileTime and QueryPerformanceCounter. pyproject allows >= 3.11, the CI matrix includes windows-latest with 3.11, and the production tree is on a Windows drive (runtime is open item U-08). receive_time_ns, the section 3.1 end-to-end delay decision_time_ns - as_of_time_ns and second-scale lead/lag would then be quantised far above the 1/5/20 ms targets, and many ticks would share one receive time. LatencyRecorder (perf_counter_ns) is not affected. Not verifiable in this Linux container.
findings.proposed_change: Derive now_ns from one wall-clock anchor plus perf_counter_ns deltas (still clamped against regression), or require Python >= 3.13 on Windows. Record the measured clock resolution in the session 01 feed benchmark.

findings.area: Prefix invariance and replay comparison (S02-ACC-01, S01-ACC-08); identity.run_id; RecordSink
findings.title: What is compared in a prefix-invariance or replay test is not defined, and streams are not run-scoped
findings.detail: Section 3.1 l.97-99 defines prefix invariance by a time watermark. (a) Every Evidence embeds run_id, and the run configuration hash 'must cover data range, seeds, parameters and code commit' (gie/contracts/identity.py:20-26). The truncated-input run of S02-ACC-01, and any run after a new commit, therefore has another run_id and the records are not byte-equal although nothing causal changed. (b) Stream names are <contract>/<producer> without run scope, while RecordSink.publish is 'idempotent per (stream, seq)' and raises SequenceConflictError on different content (interfaces.py:36-44); two runs into one sink collide at seq 0. (c) With equal receive times the watermark does not identify the last input. (d) Producers have no uniform way to obtain run_id, mode, clock and sinks.
findings.proposed_change: Define the S02-ACC-01 comparison as equality of canonical bytes under the same run configuration with the input iterator truncated after input k (identified by its EventKey), or exclude run_id from the comparison. State that a RecordSink or journal belongs to exactly one run_id. Provide a shared RunContext (run_id, mode, clock, scheduler, parameters, sinks).

findings.area: Beyond the specification: tick storage, provenance, package allow-list, feature dictionary
findings.title: Suggestions that the specification does not require
findings.detail: (a) Section 7 l.265: 'Canonical bytes are what is journaled'. A canonical Tick is about 270 bytes; encode, decode and fingerprint each cost about 25-29 microseconds at p50 in this container with the synthetic sample. That is well inside the 1 ms tick target but only about 40k ticks per second for history scans, and SequenceTracker needs a fingerprint on every observe, recomputed by each TickSink consumer. (b) Tick keeps neither the raw source timestamp or UTC offset applied (a wrong broker-time/DST conversion cannot be repaired once records are 'never modified') nor the broker's symbol name; DataOrigin.BROKER_FEED is a misnomer for vendor feeds. (c) dependency_graph.yaml third_party (l.91-93) lists only gie.core and gie.contracts; what gie.market_data and gie.intermarket may import (read-only broker SDK, columnar storage, numeric libraries) is undefined. (d) The feature dictionary (S02-DEL-01) has no defined location or format, although ModelVersion.feature_schema_sha256 hashes it and kinds, roles and feature names are open strings that the 'unknown vocabulary is refused' rule does not cover.
findings.proposed_change: State that 01 may use any storage encoding from which the canonical bytes are reproduced exactly, checked by a round-trip test. Add optional Tick fields source_time_offset_s and source_symbol, or state that 01 keeps them in its own store. Add a per-package third-party allow-list. Fix a location and canonical format for feature dictionaries and let producers validate kinds, roles and feature names against them.

findings.area: Candidate / TradePlan; S04-ASG-01, S04-ASG-08, S04-ASG-10, S05-ASG-05, S05-ASG-13, S05-ACC-05, G02-03
findings.title: Candidate estimates are in R but the Candidate defines no risk unit; 05 cannot derive plan-level expected net R
findings.detail: Owner spec, brief 04: 'Train regularized net-R and payoff models ... estimate uncertainty, holding time and expected costs'. Brief 05: 'Construct alternative market/limit/retest/pullback plans with executable entry, hard invalidation, realistic destination, expected net R and uncertainty'. /home/user/Hello/specifications/SHARED_CONTRACTS.md:62 defines an R multiple as 'result divided by the amount initially risked', and /home/user/Hello/specifications/contracts/FIELDS.md:10 says Candidate estimates are 'expressed in R (multiples of the amount risked)'. Candidate (FIELDS.md:12-42) carries only reference_price: no stop, invalidation level or risk distance (checked: no Candidate field name contains stop, risk or invalid). The amount risked exists only per plan (/home/user/Hello/gie/contracts/trade_plan.py:259, risk_per_unit = |entry - stop|) and differs for every alternative. TradePlan.expected_net_r, net_r_stdev and expected_cost_r are required non-null (FIELDS.md:362-364). 05 may not import gie.prediction (/home/user/Hello/specifications/dependency_graph.yaml:80-81), and /home/user/Hello/gie/contracts/interfaces.py:29-104 offers no prediction call. So 05 must rescale candidate R figures, and expected_cost_r (a price cost divided by an unknown distance), with an unknown denominator. The positive expectancy gate and calibration against realised Position.net_r are then computed on numbers with no defined unit. Neither session may fix this locally (COM-06).
findings.proposed_change: Add to Candidate a field risk_unit_price (decimal > 0: the price distance equal to 1R in all *_r fields; set if and only if scored, extend CND-2), or reference_stop_price. Define in SHARED_CONTRACTS section 2 how plan-level R is derived from it. Either add a synchronous PlanScorer Protocol (implemented by 04, called by 05 with entry, stop and targets; no training) or state that 05 derives plan estimates only by that documented rescaling. State whether TradePlan.model_version_id names 04's model or 05's scoring mapping.

findings.area: identity.alternative_group_id / candidate_id / Candidate.evidence_ids; S05-ACC-04, G02-02
findings.title: Opportunity identity is unstable: alternative groups and candidate ids change with every revision and differ per engine for the same market event
findings.detail: FIELDS.md:338: 'Plans that share alternative_group_id are mutually exclusive ways to trade the same candidate: at most one of them may ever be executed.' /home/user/Hello/gie/contracts/identity.py:47-57: evidence_id includes revision; candidate_id = f(setup_type, side, evidence_ids, revision); alternative_group_id = f(candidate_id). Verified in memory: (1) a plan built on candidate revision 1 has a different alternative_group_id from a plan built on revision 0 of the same opportunity; (2) an evidence revision (stage TRIGGERED to CONFIRMED) changes evidence_id and therefore candidate_id, and nothing says whether that is a new candidate or revision+1; (3) two engines observing the same market event (equal market_event_id) give candidates {A}, {B} and {A,B} with three distinct ids and three distinct groups, although /home/user/Hello/specifications/SHARED_CONTRACTS.md:170-171 says they 'MUST be counted once downstream'. Candidate accepts both evidence ids ('already de-duplicated' at /home/user/Hello/gie/contracts/candidate.py:114 is prose only), and the representative to keep is unspecified. So 07/08 cannot enforce exclusivity or 'Duplicate plan handling' from ids. No enforcer is named: RiskGate.evaluate reserves risk per plan (interfaces.py:48-58), so evaluating two alternatives reserves twice; OrderEvent has no group id; 05 is not a consumer of OrderEvent or Position (SHARED_CONTRACTS.md:31-32).
findings.proposed_change: Introduce a stable opportunity_id = f(setup_type, side, horizon, sorted market_event_ids), independent of evidence and candidate revisions and of the observing engine, and carry it on Candidate and TradePlan. Define alternative_group_id = f(opportunity_id). Specify how evidence of one market event from several engines is listed and counted. Add alternative_group_id to ENTRY OrderEvents and name the enforcer (08 reserves once per group, 07 refuses a second entry of a group). Add 05 as consumer of OrderEvent and Position.

findings.area: identity.candidate_id and derived ids; G01-02, S04-ASG-11, S04-ASG-12, S09-ASG-09
findings.title: candidate_id omits horizon and model, so scalp/intraday, baseline and shadow scorers produce different records with the same id, and plan, risk and order ids inherit the collision
findings.detail: /home/user/Hello/gie/contracts/identity.py:51-52: candidate_id = make_id('cnd', setup_type, side, sorted(evidence_ids), revision). Candidate.horizon (/home/user/Hello/gie/contracts/candidate.py:103) and model_version_id are not identity parts. Verified: the same setup, side and evidence scored as INTRADAY instead of SCALP, or by another model version, gives an identical candidate_id with a different fingerprint. The owner spec needs all three cases: 'hybrid scalping and intraday' (G01), 'Compare against GCE-B and simple baselines' (brief 04), 'shadow compare' (brief 09). The collision cascades through plan_id(candidate_id, ...), risk_decision_id(run, plan_id, attempt) and client_order_id(run, plan_id, intent, attempt) (identity.py:60-79). Because 'Orders are idempotent by identity' (/home/user/Hello/specifications/SHARED_CONTRACTS.md:172), an order for the second scorer's plan would be treated as a duplicate of the first.
findings.proposed_change: Add horizon and a scorer discriminator (model_version_id, or a scorer role) to the candidate identity parts. Alternatively state normatively that a run has exactly one scorer per (setup_type, side, evidence set) and that baselines and shadow models run only as separate runs. In either case document how paired comparison across scorers is keyed (see the opportunity_id proposal).

findings.area: Candidate / TradePlan / RiskGate / ModelRegistry / streams; G07-08, G07-09, G07-10, G07-12, S09-ASG-09
findings.title: Owner-approved promotion is enforced only on the registry record: any model (shadow, research, unknown) can drive a SELECTED plan and be approved, and shadow output cannot be separated
findings.detail: Master G07: 'Background research isolated from active model; shadow validation, versioned promotion with owner approval and rollback. No untested online changes.' /home/user/Hello/specifications/SHARED_CONTRACTS.md:326 constrains only ModelVersion. Verified: a TradePlan with status SELECTED citing a model id that exists in no registry is valid, and an APPROVED RiskDecision for it is valid. Nothing on Candidate or TradePlan records whether the model was ACTIVE, SHADOW or RESEARCH at decision time. ModelRegistry (/home/user/Hello/gie/contracts/interfaces.py:95-104) has get and active(kind) only: no status as of a past instant, and no way for 04 to learn which versions are in SHADOW. A parallel shadow run cannot share a sink: stream names carry no run id (/home/user/Hello/gie/contracts/ordering.py:27-40), RecordSink is idempotent 'per (stream, seq)' (interfaces.py:39), and SequenceTracker raised GIE.SEQ.CONFLICT for a second run's record at the same (stream, seq).
findings.proposed_change: Add model_status (ModelStatus as of decision time) to Candidate and TradePlan. Add the rule to SHARED_CONTRACTS section 9 that in a PAPER run a plan may be ARMED/SELECTED and approved only when model_status is ACTIVE, with REPLAY research runs exempt. Define shadow operation as a separate run_id and make stream identity (run_id, stream) in RecordSink and SequenceTracker. Add a by-status lookup to ModelRegistry.

findings.area: missing Decision record; S05-ASG-09..12, S05-ACC-01, S05-DEL-03, S09-ASG-01, S09-ASG-02, G07-04, G07-07
findings.title: No record can hold a ranking decision or a candidate-level rejection, and ownership of Candidate REJECTED is undefined
findings.detail: Brief 05: 'Rank only currently available candidates, reject stale/negative expected opportunities; one unified decision stream'. Brief 09: 'Collect decision and outcome logs, rejected/missed setups'. /home/user/Hello/specifications/SHARED_CONTRACTS.md:199-201 says a candidate failing the expectancy gate is 'an ordinary record with REJECTED status'. (1) Line 28 names 04 as the only Candidate producer, but the gate is 05's assignment. If 05 emits the REJECTED revision, its revision 1 and 04's own revision 1 share a candidate_id with different content (verified; the id has no producer part). (2) A candidate rejected before a plan exists cannot be a TradePlan: stop, at least one target and non-null expected_net_r, net_r_stdev and model_version_id are required (verified: a REJECTED plan for an unscored candidate fails 'expected_net_r: must be a number'), so recording it would mean inventing geometry. (3) No record holds one ranking pass: the candidates considered, their scores, the selected plan or 'no trade'. 'No future candidate ranking' is therefore not auditable from records, and 09 cannot build decision logs or separate decision quality from outcomes without 05's internals, which it may not import. (4) PLN-9 forbids reason codes on usable plans (verified), so why a plan is selected or still waiting cannot be recorded.
findings.proposed_change: Add a Decision contract (stream decision/<producer>, new id prefix): decision and as-of times, candidate_ids considered, ranked plan_ids with score, selected_plan_id or null, rejected items with reason codes, risk decision id or null. State in section 1 that only 04 emits Candidate records and that 05 expresses candidate rejections through Decision. Allow informational reason codes on usable plans. Required before 05 can deliver 'one unified decision stream' and before 09 can collect decision logs.

findings.area: missing Outcome / label record; S04-ASG-01, S04-ASG-02, S04-ACC-01, S04-ACC-02, S09-ASG-01, S09-ASG-02, G07-04, G07-07
findings.title: No shared outcome record: training labels, counterfactual results of rejected/missed setups and label availability times have no contract
findings.detail: Brief 04: 'Train regularized net-R and payoff models', acceptance 'Purged chronological splits, calibration by setup and session'. Brief 09: 'Collect decision and outcome logs, rejected/missed setups'. Master G07: 'Separate decision quality from outcomes'. The only realised result in the contracts is the closed Position of an executed GIE trade (/home/user/Hello/gie/contracts/position.py:207-215, net_r). There is no record for the outcome of a historical setup used for training, for the counterfactual result of a rejected or missed candidate, for the label definition (exit rule and cost model behind a net-R label), or for the instant a label became known. Without a label end time, purging and 'prior-only neighbors' cannot be verified from data. Sessions 04, 09 and 10 may not import each other (/home/user/Hello/specifications/dependency_graph.yaml:80-86), so each would define its own incompatible label format.
findings.proposed_change: Add an Outcome contract: subject (candidate_id, plan_id or position_id), kind REALIZED or COUNTERFACTUAL, label specification id (exit rule and cost-model version), entry and exit times, label_end_time_ns (availability instant), realised net R with its risk unit, MFE and MAE in R, holding time, exit reason, data_origin. Realised outcomes come from 07, counterfactual ones from 10/09. I believe this contract is REQUIRED before 04 can train and before 09 can start.

findings.area: Candidate / ModelVersion leakage provenance; S04-ASG-06, S04-ASG-07, S04-ACC-03, S09-ACC-03, G10-01, G10-02, G10-03
