findings.title: Leakage is only partly detectable from records: fit window only, via a registry join; nothing for label windows, embargo, transforms, model selection or neighbours
findings.detail: Brief 04: 'Use prior-only neighbors and training-only transforms', acceptance 'leakage mutation tests'. The only provenance is Candidate.model_version_id pointing to ModelVersion.training_data_start_ns/end_ns (/home/user/Hello/specifications/contracts/FIELDS.md:142-143, 'Latest event time used for fitting; predictions for earlier instants are in-sample'). (1) Verified: a Candidate decided 30 days before its model's training_data_end_ns is valid and unmarked; the check needs a registry join and exists neither as rule nor helper. (2) 'Event time used for fitting' does not cover outcome windows (a sample at t whose label is known at t + holding time), embargo length, data used for hyper-parameter selection or early stopping, or the fit window of transforms. (3) Candidate carries no neighbour provenance (count, newest neighbour's label end, memory cutoff), so 'prior-only' cannot be verified per prediction, and a memory that grows after the artifact was frozen is not bounded by artifact_sha256. (4) The field doc says the window is 'null for rule sets', but tuned rulesets such as GCE-B thresholds are fitted to data (G09: 'no corrected statistical significance').
findings.proposed_change: Redefine training_data_end_ns as the latest availability instant of any information used to produce the artifact (labels, transforms, feature selection, hyper-parameter selection); null only when no data was used. Add optional embargo_ns and split_spec_sha256 to ModelVersion. Add to Candidate model_information_end_ns (for similarity models the newest neighbour label end actually used), neighbor_count and in_sample, with an invariant tying in_sample to model_information_end_ns >= as_of_time_ns. Add a helper is_out_of_sample(candidate, model) to gie.contracts.

findings.area: ModelVersion MDL-6, parent_model_version_id, MODEL_STATUS_TRANSITIONS; S09-ASG-11, S09-ACC-05, G07-11
findings.title: Rollback target is conflated with lineage and fixed at registration; re-activation of a RETIRED version is not tied to a rollback
findings.detail: /home/user/Hello/specifications/contracts/FIELDS.md:146 defines parent_model_version_id as 'Version this one was derived from, and the rollback target'. It is immutable from revision 0 (/home/user/Hello/gie/contracts/model_version.py:214-229), and MDL-6 (model_version.py:202-204) requires it for ROLLED_BACK. The version to roll back to is whichever was ACTIVE when this one was promoted. That is unknown at registration and need not be the lineage parent. Verified: (1) a version trained from scratch (parent null) can never be ROLLED_BACK, only RETIRED, and a RETIRED version can be re-activated, unlike a ROLLED_BACK one; (2) a version whose parent was never ACTIVE can be ROLLED_BACK 'to' it; (3) validate_model_transition accepts RETIRED -> ACTIVE for any retired version with approved_by='anyone' and a reused decision id, with no successor rolled back, although the comment at model_version.py:59-61 says rollback is 'the only way a RETIRED version becomes ACTIVE again'. No rule states that at most one version per kind or family is ACTIVE, or the order of the two records that make up a promotion or rollback.
findings.proposed_change: Split the field into derived_from_model_version_id (immutable lineage) and replaces_model_version_id (recorded on the ACTIVE revision: the version that was ACTIVE before). Make MDL-6 require the latter, or an explicit 'rollback to no model'. Add a registry-level validator over the whole history: RETIRED -> ACTIVE only when the entry cites a ROLLED_BACK successor; at most one ACTIVE per (kind, model_name); defined record order for promotion and rollback.

findings.area: interfaces.ModelRegistry / ModelKind.COMPOSITE; S04-DEL-02, S09-ASG-08, S09-ASG-09, G02-03, G07-02
findings.title: ModelRegistry is read-only and allows one active version per kind: 04 cannot register artifacts, and per-setup models, shadow listing and status history are not expressible
findings.detail: /home/user/Hello/gie/contracts/interfaces.py:95-104: the Protocol has get(model_version_id) and active(kind) -> ModelVersion | None, 'implemented by 09; read by 04, 05, 08, 11'. (1) 04 trains and freezes artifacts (brief 04: 'Frozen artifacts') but may not import gie.learning and has no register or transition call. (2) active(kind) returns a single version per ModelKind, while the owner spec asks for 'setup-specific expected net R' and 'setup-specific return models'. Several families of one kind cannot be active together, and COMPOSITE has no component list in ModelVersion (/home/user/Hello/specifications/contracts/FIELDS.md:127-150). (3) No listing by status, so SHADOW versions cannot be found for shadow scoring. (4) get does not say which revision it returns and offers no status as of a past instant, so 08's quality_validated or a later audit cannot be re-checked. (5) No snapshot: two calls within one scoring pass can straddle a promotion.
findings.proposed_change: Extend the Protocol: register(entry), transition(entry), history(model_version_id), find(kind, status, model_name=None), status_at(model_version_id, time_ns), and snapshot() returning an immutable view. Key the active lookup by (kind, model_name) or an explicit scope. Add component_model_version_ids to ModelVersion for COMPOSITE.

findings.area: ModelVersion header and provenance; COM-07, M-AUTH-07, S04-ACC-06, S09-ACC-06, M-GATE-05, G10-01
findings.title: ModelVersion sits outside the run/origin/time model: no data_origin, no dataset or configuration identity, wall-clock ordering that cannot coexist with replay time
findings.detail: /home/user/Hello/specifications/SHARED_CONTRACTS.md:327 lists as structural: 'Every record names its run, mode and the origin of its data (fixtures are labelled)'. ModelVersion extends Sequenced only (/home/user/Hello/gie/contracts/model_version.py:89): no run_id, mode or data_origin (verified from FIELD_SPECS). A model fitted on SYNTHETIC_FIXTURE data, with headline metrics such as oos_mean_net_r (/home/user/Hello/tests/gie/samples.py:126), carries no fixture label and can reach ACTIVE; Candidate.data_origin covers only the market data of the candidate. Reproducibility is an acceptance test of 04 and 09, but the record identifies training data only by a time range plus seed and code_commit: no dataset manifest hash, training-configuration hash or environment lock. Time: ModelVersion is ordered by status_time_ns (/home/user/Hello/gie/contracts/ordering.py:56-57), a wall reading, while a REPLAY run uses virtual time. MDL-4 rejects a status stamped earlier than created_time_ns (verified), so a walk-forward model schedule inside a replay cannot be represented.
findings.proposed_change: Add training_data_origin (DataOrigin; null only when no data was used), training_data_sha256 (hash of a dataset manifest) and training_config_sha256. State that ModelVersion times are always SYSTEM clock readings. State that a replay takes its per-run model schedule from the run configuration (covered by run_id), not from registry status, and exclude ModelVersion from the per-run total order or define its place in it.

findings.area: ModelVersion promotion evidence; S09-ACC-04, S09-DEL-03, S09-DEL-04, S04-DEL-01, S04-DEL-06, G07-09, G07-10
findings.title: ACTIVE requires only two free-text approval fields: no shadow evidence, criteria or report link, and no reason for REJECTED, ROLLED_BACK or RETIRED
findings.detail: Brief 09 acceptance: 'promotion rejection for weak evidence'; deliverables 'shadow results, promotion criteria'. Brief 04 deliverables: 'Model cards ... unsuccessful models'. MDL-2 (/home/user/Hello/gie/contracts/model_version.py:171-176) requires approved_by (any string up to 64 characters) and approval_reference (pattern ^D-[0-9]{3,5}$) and nothing else. Verified: RESEARCH -> SHADOW -> ACTIVE with identical status_time_ns and empty metrics passes the record invariants and validate_model_transition, so 'shadow validation' is enforced only as a label sequence. ModelVersion has no reason field, so why a version was REJECTED, ROLLED_BACK or RETIRED cannot be recorded. metrics is at most 64 name-to-float pairs (model_version.py:144-153), too few for calibration by setup and session, and its doc says 'full results live in the model card', but there is no model card or evaluation report reference, no shadow run ids and no promotion-criteria version.
findings.proposed_change: Add status_reasons (reason codes, required for REJECTED, ROLLED_BACK and RETIRED). Add evaluation_report_uri and evaluation_report_sha256 (model card or shadow report), shadow_run_ids (list of run ids) and promotion_criteria_sha256, required on a revision that enters ACTIVE from SHADOW. Add the rule that the registry (09) refuses the transition when the cited report does not exist or does not match its hash.

findings.area: event ordering, StreamRank; S00-ASG-25, S05-ACC-01, S10-ACC-02, S09-ASG-01
findings.title: Stream ranks invert cause and effect for records created at the same instant
findings.detail: /home/user/Hello/specifications/SHARED_CONTRACTS.md:228-235: 'All records of a run are processed in ascending EventKey = (time_ns, rank, stream, seq)' with ranks tick, order event, position, risk decision, evidence, candidate, trade plan (/home/user/Hello/gie/core/ordering.py:42-54). The data flow at SHARED_CONTRACTS.md:37 is Tick -> Evidence -> Candidate -> TradePlan -> RiskDecision -> OrderEvent -> Position. A ReplayClock moves only when the driver advances it (section 3.2), so without modelled latency a full cascade shares one instant. Verified with the sample records at one instant: order event (20) < position (30) < risk decision (40) < evidence (50) < candidate (60) < trade plan (70). A consumer that follows the rule (09 logs, 10, 11, 12) sees the entry request and the RiskDecision before the plan, candidate and evidence they refer to. A look-ahead check of the form 'a record may only reference records earlier in the total order' then fails on legitimate records, or must exempt equal timestamps, which is where candle-close leaks occur. The stated rationale ('Execution facts therefore precede intelligence derived at the same instant') holds for inbound broker reports but not for GIE's own *_REQUESTED events and decisions.
findings.proposed_change: Keep inbound facts first (clock, ticks, broker reports) and break remaining ties by causal emission order. Options: a run-wide emission counter assigned by the journal and placed before rank in EventKey; or ranks that follow data-flow depth for GIE-produced records (evidence, candidate, trade plan, risk decision, order request, position), with requests distinguished from reports. State the chosen rule in section 6.2 and add a same-instant cascade to the ordering tests.

findings.area: PlanStatus / CandidateStatus lifecycle; S05-ASG-08, S05-ACC-02, S07 acceptance 'stale plans', G04-11
findings.title: Plan and candidate statuses have no definitions, transition table or validator; the effect of a new revision on existing approvals and working orders is undefined
findings.detail: /home/user/Hello/specifications/contracts/FIELDS.md:571-575 lists PlanStatus values PREPARED, ARMED, SELECTED, WITHDRAWN, EXPIRED, REJECTED without meaning or transitions, while orders and models have tables (FIELDS.md:637-688). /home/user/Hello/specifications/SHARED_CONTRACTS.md:195-196 names validators for order, position and model only (verified: gie.contracts has no validate_plan_transition or validate_candidate_transition). Verified: a plan revision may move the stop from 2647.80 to 2640.00 although the field doc says 'It may later be tightened, never widened' (FIELDS.md:360), and a chain REJECTED -> SELECTED is constructible. Undefined: which status RiskGate.evaluate expects, which status 07 needs before submitting, who emits EXPIRED, and whether a new revision voids the RiskDecision, reservation and working order bound to the old plan_id. Revision is part of plan_id, and RiskDecision.plan_id and the order's plan_id are fixed, so every re-score orphans them.
findings.proposed_change: Define each status in SHARED_CONTRACTS. Add PLAN_STATUS_TRANSITIONS and CANDIDATE_STATUS_TRANSITIONS with validate_plan_transition and validate_candidate_transition: immutable opportunity, side, entry_style and variant; stop never further from the entry; REJECTED, WITHDRAWN and EXPIRED final. State what a superseding revision does to approvals, reservations and working orders of the superseded plan_id, and which statuses 08 and 07 require.

findings.area: freshness / causality across records; S00-ASG-23, G03-11, G03-12, S05-ASG-10, S09-ASG-03
findings.title: Expiry does not propagate to derived records, as_of_time_ns is undefined for inputs that have no receive time, and age limits have no parameters
findings.detail: (1) /home/user/Hello/specifications/SHARED_CONTRACTS.md:127-137 defines expiry per record only. Verified: a TradePlan valid one hour beyond its Candidate's valid_until_ns is valid. A consumer that checks only the plan (07, 'stale plans') acts on an expired candidate or evidence. The relation between RiskDecision.valid_until_ns and a resting entry order's valid_until_ns is also undefined. (2) Lines 95-96 define as_of_time_ns as 'the receive time of the newest input it depends on'. A TradePlan's inputs are a Candidate and a RiskDecision, which have no receive time. Reading it as the direct input's availability (decision_time_ns) or as the transitive market-data watermark gives different values, so a cross-record causality check and 'End-to-end delay of a decision is decision_time_ns - as_of_time_ns' (line 101) are not comparable between subsystems. (3) Line 130 calls 'max_age_ns per feed and per decision stage' research parameters, but /home/user/Hello/specifications/research_parameters.toml:13-61 contains none and nothing says which field is the reference instant of a Candidate or TradePlan. The file is owned by session 00, with no documented way for 04, 05 or 09 to add parameters (expectancy threshold, embargo, promotion criteria).
findings.proposed_change: Add normative rules: valid_until_ns of a derived record must not exceed the minimum valid_until_ns of its inputs; entry order expiry <= approval expiry <= plan expiry. Define as_of_time_ns as the maximum ordering time of the direct inputs and add a helper assert_causal(child, *inputs). If end-to-end delay is to be read from records, add a separate market-data watermark field. Define the reference instant for age checks per contract and a namespaced procedure for session-specific research parameters.

findings.area: TradePlan PLN-3, PLN-6, entry fields; S05-ASG-01, S05-ASG-02, S05-ASG-08, G03-01
findings.title: Retest/pullback plans executed by market order cannot carry their entry level, trigger or pre-entry invalidation; PLN-3 and PLN-6 reject legitimate plans
findings.detail: Brief 05: 'alternative market/limit/retest/pullback plans with executable entry ... actual behavior invalidates plans'. PLN-3 (/home/user/Hello/gie/contracts/trade_plan.py:206-209) forces entry_price to null whenever entry_order_type is MARKET, and geometry then uses reference_price, the 'Executable price at decision time' (trade_plan.py:93-94; /home/user/Hello/specifications/contracts/FIELDS.md:359). Verified: a BUY PULLBACK plan entered by market order on confirmation cannot state its pullback level (PLN-3 violation). The same plan with a first target at 2650.00, above the intended entry near 2648 but below the quote 2650.35 at preparation time, is rejected by PLN-6. A prepared plan has no machine-readable trigger or pre-entry invalidation condition, only valid_until_ns, max_spread and max_entry_slippage, although Evidence already has an Invalidation value object (FIELDS.md:421-434). 08 therefore sizes and 07 checks against a reference price that is stale by the time the plan triggers, and 'actual behavior invalidates plans' cannot be declared in the plan or tested downstream.
findings.proposed_change: Allow entry_price as the intended entry level for RETEST and PULLBACK regardless of order type (restrict PLN-3 to entry_style MARKET) and evaluate PLN-5 and PLN-6 against it. Add optional entry_trigger and invalidations (list) to TradePlan, reusing the price, trigger, basis and timeframe structure of Invalidation. State that a triggered market plan is re-issued as a new revision with a fresh reference_price before risk evaluation.

findings.area: Candidate.net_r_stdev, TradePlan.net_r_stdev, CND-2; G02-04, S04-ASG-08, S05-ASG-13, S05-ACC-05, G04-08
findings.title: 'Uncertainty' is fixed as the outcome standard deviation only; uncertainty of the estimate and its support cannot be carried, and stdev is mandatory
findings.detail: Master G02: 'Build setup-specific expected net R, uncertainty'; brief 04: 'estimate uncertainty'. The owner spec does not say which uncertainty is meant. The contract silently picks one reading: net_r_stdev is the 'Predictive standard deviation of the net result' (/home/user/Hello/specifications/contracts/FIELDS.md:33 and :363), the dispersion of a single trade outcome. No field carries the uncertainty of expected_net_r itself (standard error or interval) or its support (effective sample size, neighbour count). That is the quantity a positive expectancy gate, or 'adaptive sizing only from validated quality', would use. A trade with outcomes -1R and +2R has a stdev near 1.4R however well its mean is known. Implementers of 04, 05 and 08 will read different meanings into the same field. CND-2 (/home/user/Hello/gie/contracts/candidate.py:171-183) also makes stdev mandatory for every scored candidate (verified: a candidate with quantiles and no stdev is rejected) while quantiles are optional, and TradePlan can carry only the stdev.
findings.proposed_change: Decide and document the meaning; this needs the owner or supervisor because the specification is silent. Suggested: keep net_r_stdev as outcome dispersion; add optional expected_net_r_stderr (>= 0) and support_count (integer >= 0) to Candidate and TradePlan; relax CND-2 to 'scored means expected_net_r plus at least one of net_r_stdev or two or more quantiles'.

findings.area: Destination / Target / payoff outputs; S04-ASG-02, S04-ASG-05, S05-ASG-04, G02-05
findings.title: Destination probabilities have no defined event or horizon, payoff-model outputs have no fields, and plan targets are not linked to predicted destinations
findings.detail: Brief 04: 'payoff models ... scenario destinations'; brief 05: 'realistic destination'. Destination (/home/user/Hello/specifications/contracts/FIELDS.md:401-410) is 'A price the market may travel to under a named scenario' with label 'Scenario or destination name' and probability_frac 'Estimated probability of reaching it'. Not defined: reaching it before what (any stop, the candidate's expiry, a time horizon), whether probabilities are exclusive scenario probabilities or independent touch probabilities, and whether adverse destinations are allowed. One label conflates scenario and destination, and labels are not unique (/home/user/Hello/gie/contracts/candidate.py:149-150 has no uniqueness rule). 05 cannot convert destinations into targets or expected R consistently. ModelKind has PAYOFF_MODEL, but Candidate has no payoff output (expected win and loss size, favourable or adverse excursion); win_probability_frac and expected_net_r do not determine the payoff. Target (FIELDS.md:463-471) has label, price and close_frac only, so whether a target is 'realistic' cannot be read from a plan.
findings.proposed_change: Define probability_frac normatively (suggested: probability that the executable price touches the price within horizon_ns, not conditional on any stop). Add scenario (code) and horizon_ns to Destination, with unique (scenario, label). Add optional expected_win_r and expected_loss_r (in the candidate's risk unit) to Candidate. Add optional destination_label and reach_probability_frac to Target.

findings.area: Evidence scores for non-gold instruments; G06-08, G06-09, S04-DEP-01 (03 optional), S03
findings.title: Direction reference of bullish/bearish scores is undefined for evidence about instruments other than XAUUSD
findings.detail: /home/user/Hello/specifications/SHARED_CONTRACTS.md:78-79: 'Tick and Evidence may describe other observed instruments'. Evidence.symbol is the 'Instrument the observation is about' (/home/user/Hello/gie/contracts/evidence.py:155) and bullish_score the 'Strength of bullish evidence' (/home/user/Hello/specifications/contracts/FIELDS.md:98). For evidence about DXY it is not stated whether 'bullish' means DXY rising or gold rising. The sample at /home/user/Hello/tests/gie/samples.py:603-616 (symbol DXY, bearish_score 0.3) does not settle it. Master G06 says 'Learn conditional lead/lag, never assume fixed correlations', which argues for scores about the observed instrument, while G02 speaks of 'directional scores' in a gold context. 04 consumes 03's evidence as model features; if 03 and 04 assume different conventions the feature sign flips silently, and no record lets 04 detect it. Related: PriceLevel.price and Invalidation.price are documented as 'USD per troy ounce' (FIELDS.md:427, :452) although they may belong to non-gold evidence.
findings.proposed_change: State normatively in SHARED_CONTRACTS section 2 that Evidence scores, levels and invalidation always describe the instrument named in symbol and are never pre-translated into a gold direction; the mapping to gold is learned by 04. Alternatively add an explicit direction_reference_symbol field. Change the unit text of PriceLevel.price and Invalidation.price to 'quote currency per unit'.

findings.area: interfaces and data-flow table; S05-ASG-02, S05-ASG-12, G03-03, S09-ASG-01
findings.title: 04 and 05 are not Tick consumers, 05 never sees OrderEvent or Position, and there is no interface to read records back
findings.detail: /home/user/Hello/specifications/SHARED_CONTRACTS.md:26 lists Tick consumers as '02, 03, 06, 07, 10, 11', and the TickSink docstring says 'implemented by 02, 03, 06, 07, 10' (/home/user/Hello/gie/contracts/interfaces.py:30). Yet Candidate.reference_price and TradePlan.reference_price must be the 'Executable price at decision time: ask for BUY, bid for SELL' (/home/user/Hello/specifications/contracts/FIELDS.md:28 and :359), and /home/user/Hello/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:18 places 05 in 'TACTICAL (05, 07, 08) every tick or second'. Lines 31-32 of the table omit 05 as consumer of OrderEvent and Position, so 05 cannot learn that a selected plan was filled, rejected or closed. For records the only interface is RecordSink.publish (interfaces.py:36-44). There is no way to subscribe to a stream or read a journal; ARCHITECTURE.md:125 leaves 'the storage engine' to sessions 01/07. 09 must 'Collect decision and outcome logs' from finished runs, including those of 10, and may import neither storage implementation.
findings.proposed_change: Add 04, 05 and 08 as Tick consumers and 05 as consumer of OrderEvent and Position, in the table and the TickSink docstring. State that a subsystem's input port is its own RecordSink implementation wired by gie.app. Add a RecordSource Protocol (streams(run_id); read(run_id, stream, from_seq) returning records in sequence order) and specify the journal layout it reads. I believe RecordSource is REQUIRED before 09 (and 10, 11) can start.

findings.area: additional shared contracts and artifacts; CR-003, U-11, COM-06, S04-ACC-02, S04-ASG-10, S05-ASG-02, S09-ASG-03, S09-ASG-05, S09-DEL-01
findings.title: CR-003 does not cover what sessions 04, 05 and 09 need before they can start
findings.detail: /home/user/Hello/docs/CHANGE_REQUESTS.md:82-96 (CR-003) expects Candle, BrokerCalendar, InstrumentSpec and AccountSnapshot from sessions 01, 07 and 08. From this lens the following are REQUIRED and unowned. 04: Candle; a session classifier, because Candidate.session is the 'Broker session at decision time' and acceptance asks 'calibration by setup and session'; InstrumentSpec with cost schedule for 'expected costs'; a machine-readable feature dictionary with a defined hash, since ModelVersion.feature_schema_sha256 is the 'Hash of the feature dictionary the model expects' (/home/user/Hello/specifications/contracts/FIELDS.md:144) but no such artifact or format exists and Evidence carries no dictionary version, so training/serving skew is undetectable. 05: InstrumentSpec (tick size, minimum stop distance) for 'executable entry'; BrokerCalendar for rollover and weekend (overnight_allowed: 'never over a weekend'). 09: a RunManifest, because run_id is an opaque hash of the configuration (/home/user/Hello/gie/contracts/identity.py:20-26) and data range, seeds, code commit and parameters cannot be recovered for the 'Experiment registry' or reproducibility; record types for latency and errors, because LatencySummary (/home/user/Hello/gie/core/latency.py:26) and GieError.to_dict (/home/user/Hello/gie/core/errors.py:35) are not contracts and cannot pass through RecordSink, so 09 cannot 'Collect ... latency ... and execution errors' from other subsystems. Outcome, Decision and RecordSource are covered in separate findings.
findings.proposed_change: Extend CR-003 and U-11 with owners and deadlines. Before wave 3 (04, 05): Candle, BrokerCalendar/session classifier, InstrumentSpec with cost schedule, FeatureDictionary artifact with canonical hash, Outcome, Decision. Before wave 4 (09): RunManifest, RecordSource, LatencyReport, ErrorEvent. Record in the dependency graph which session proposes each.

findings.area: TradePlan invariants; S05-ASG-11, S05-ACC-05
findings.title: A SELECTED or ARMED plan with negative expected net R is constructible and approvable
findings.detail: Brief 05: 'reject stale/negative expected opportunities', acceptance 'Positive expectancy gate'. Verified in memory: TradePlan with status SELECTED and expected_net_r = -0.5, and one with status ARMED and expected_net_r = -2.0, pass all invariants (/home/user/Hello/gie/contracts/trade_plan.py:192-251), and an APPROVED RiskDecision for the former is valid. /home/user/Hello/specifications/SHARED_CONTRACTS.md:309-327 lists the rules made structural under decision D-012; this unconditional rule of the owner spec is not among them, so 08 and 07 have no way to notice a gate failure in 05.
findings.proposed_change: Add PLN-11: when status is SELECTED (and ARMED, once defined as 'an entry may rest'), expected_net_r > 0. The research threshold above zero stays a parameter of 05. PREPARED stays unconstrained so both directions can be prepared. Add the rule to section 9.

findings.area: Evidence EVD-6 / contradicts_evidence_id; S05-ACC-03
findings.title: CONTRA evidence can reference only one evidence revision; contradicting two records produces an id collision
findings.detail: EVD-6 (/home/user/Hello/gie/contracts/evidence.py:238-240): 'contradicts_evidence_id is set if and only if state is CONTRA', a single id<evd> that includes the contradicted record's revision (/home/user/Hello/gie/contracts/identity.py:47-48). When the contradicted evidence is revised the reference goes stale. Verified: one engine and market event contradicting two evidences needs two records, and they have the same evidence_id with different content. The contract also does not say whether the scores of a CONTRA record describe the contrary direction. Brief 05 acceptance requires 'contradiction tests', which depend on these semantics.
findings.proposed_change: Replace the field with contradicts_market_event_ids (list, at least one when CONTRA), which is stable across revisions and engines, or with a list of evidence ids. State the meaning of scores in state CONTRA.

findings.area: TradePlan.contributions / EvidenceContribution; S05-ACC-07, S11 'evidence contributions'
findings.title: Plan contributions cannot be sourced from the model and cannot express non-evidence drivers
findings.detail: TradePlan.contributions holds (evidence_id, weight) pairs, 'Signed contribution to the expected net R' (/home/user/Hello/specifications/contracts/FIELDS.md:412-419). Candidate has no contributions field, and 05 cannot call 04's model (import rule; no interface), so 05 can fill the list only with its own heuristic, not with the attribution of the model that produced expected_net_r. Drivers that are not evidence records (setup prior or intercept, session, spread and cost, intermarket features) cannot be listed. No rule relates the weights to expected_net_r, so an 'explanation' can be arbitrary.
findings.proposed_change: Add contributions and baseline_r to Candidate (filled by 04) and define how 05 rescales them per plan. Allow a contribution keyed by a named feature as well as by evidence_id. Add an invariant that baseline_r plus the sum of weights equals expected_net_r within a stated tolerance when contributions are present.

findings.area: TradePlan.targets, Candidate CND-6; G04-13, S05-ASG-04, S09-ASG-02
findings.title: Small over-constraints: every plan must close volume at a fixed target, and an unscored candidate cannot say why
findings.detail: (1) targets needs at least one item and Target.close_frac must be > 0 (/home/user/Hello/gie/contracts/trade_plan.py:78 and :149). Verified: a plan whose exit is the profit ratchet alone, and a plan with an informational destination (close_frac 0), are both rejected. Brief 05 asks for a 'realistic destination', not a mandatory partial close, and master G04 specifies the 'fast monotonic profit ratchet' as an exit. /home/user/Hello/specifications/SHARED_CONTRACTS.md:313 cites G04-12 (hard protective stops) as source of the target rule, which says nothing about targets. (2) Verified: an unscored AVAILABLE candidate may not carry any reason (CND-6), so 'no active model', 'too few neighbours' and 'feature missing' are indistinguishable for the learning logs. Evidence has missing_reason for the analogous case (EVD-3).
findings.proposed_change: Allow close_frac >= 0 (0 = destination without scheduled close) while keeping at least one destination per plan. Add unscored_reason (reason code) to Candidate, set if and only if the candidate is unscored.

findings.area: Position / OrderEvent fields for learning; S09-ASG-04, S09-ASG-05, S09-ASG-12, G07-05, G07-06, G04-14
findings.title: Giveback is computable, but peak time, adverse excursion and exit reason are not recorded; the manual-trade exclusion rule is not written down
findings.detail: Profit giveback can be derived from the CLOSED snapshot (peak_net_pnl_amount minus final net P&L, /home/user/Hello/gie/contracts/position.py:132-136). For 'execution and exit learning' and the comparison 'against fixed exits' the records lack the instant of the peak, the worst executable P&L (adverse excursion) and the reason a position closed. OrderIntent.EXIT does not distinguish ratchet, time or emergency exits, and OrderEvent.reason_code is documented only as 'Reason of a rejection, cancellation, expiry or reconciliation' (/home/user/Hello/gie/contracts/order_event.py:253). PositionOwner.EXTERNAL groups manual trades with the other bots (position.py:17-23). 'No manual-trade learning' is therefore met only if learning ignores every EXTERNAL position, and no contract text says so. The first three fields go beyond the literal specification and are suggestions; the exclusion rule is a specified requirement.
findings.proposed_change: State in SHARED_CONTRACTS that learning and model fitting use only records whose position owner is GIE. Document reason_code on EXIT and protective-order requests as the exit reason. Consider adding peak_time_ns, trough_net_pnl_amount and close_reason (set if and only if CLOSED) to Position as a MINOR change.

findings.area: routing lock layer 4 / tools/check_live_lock.py / G08-03, G08-10, S00-ACC-04
findings.title: The static scan the lock depends on does not exist, so every bypass that is only detectable by scan is unmitigated
findings.detail: Spec: MASTER G08 'Never enable real execution during this project phase.'; MASTER authority 'build execution interfaces but keep real order routing disabled'. gie/core/routing_lock.py:19-20 ('4. Static scan. tools/check_live_lock.py (run in CI) fails the build if broker order-entry calls appear in GIE code or if this module is weakened'), docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:104-110 and DECISION_LOG D-011 present four independent layers. tools/ contains only benchmark_foundation.py, build_review.py, ci.py, make_golden.py, render_contract_docs.py. On a copy: 'python3 -m tools.check_live_lock' -> 'No module named tools.check_live_lock' (same for tools.check_architecture, tools.check_protected_paths, tools.gie_registers, tools.baseline_freeze, all invoked by tools/ci.py:70-118). CI reports those steps as failed (good), but layers 1-3 only constrain code that voluntarily goes through RoutingGuard: in rt1.py experiment G an object never shown to the guard received the order. Python cannot prevent that structurally, so the scan is the only control for: a second code path without authorize, a registered class that lies, monkeypatching routing_lock / RoutingGuard / _SIMULATED_ADAPTER_TYPES, object.__setattr__ on frozen records, contract subclasses, subprocess/ctypes/file-drop IPC to a terminal or the existing bots. acceptance_tests.yaml AT-S00-ACC-04 itself lists tests/gie/tools/test_check_live_lock.py and tests/gie/contracts/test_guarded_adapter.py; neither exists.
findings.proposed_change: Deliver tools/check_live_lock.py and its tests before the review gate and before any wave-2 code exists. AST based, deny by default: (a) under gie/** forbid imports of socket, ssl, http, urllib, requests, aiohttp, websockets, zmq, ctypes, subprocess, multiprocessing and any broker SDK, plus os.system/os.startfile/os.exec*; one named read-only facade module in gie/market_data is the only exemption and may not reference order-entry attribute names; (b) register_simulated_adapter referenced only from allow-listed modules; (c) no assignment/setattr/delattr to attributes of gie.core.routing_lock, RoutingGuard, GuardedExecutionAdapter, RunMode, ExecutionVenue; no access to _SIMULATED_ADAPTER_TYPES, _adapter, _member_map_, _value2member_map_; no object.__setattr__ outside gie/contracts/_spec.py; (d) no class outside gie/contracts subclasses a Record, RoutingGuard or a registered adapter; (e) .submit/.cancel/.replace called only on GuardedExecutionAdapter outside adapter modules; (f) pin the SHA-256 of routing_lock.py and guarded.py in the scan so an edit needs a reviewed change of the scan; (g) no literal containing 'ftmo_eurusd' outside tools/audit. Until it exists, change routing_lock.py:8-20 and ARCHITECTURE section 6 to 'three runtime layers; static scan not yet implemented'.

findings.area: OrderEvent / ExecutionAdapter.replace / validate_order_transition / S07-ASG-04, S06 monotonic stops, G04-11
findings.title: A replace request cannot carry the requested values, and an attached stop has no order that could be replaced
findings.detail: Spec: brief 07 'Implement ... cancel/replace ... simulated broker-side protection'; brief 06 'monotonic stops', acceptance 'no stop widening'; MASTER G04 'no ... widening protective stops'. gie/contracts/interfaces.py:73-75: 'cancel and replace [take] the corresponding *_REQUESTED event'. gie/contracts/order_event.py:395-398: for every event type other than REPLACED/RECONCILED any difference in order_type, volume_lots, limit_price, trigger_price, attached_* or valid_until_ns raises 'may only change with a REPLACED or RECONCILED event'. OrderEvent has no requested_* fields. Reproduced (rt3.py T4/T5): REPLACE_REQUESTED for a working protective SELL STOP carrying the new trigger 2649.00 (old 2647.80) -> IllegalTransitionError 'trigger_price may only change with a REPLACED or RECONCILED event'; carrying the old trigger it is valid, but then GuardedExecutionAdapter.replace (guarded.py:75-76) hands the adapter an event with no new value. Consequences: (1) S07 cannot implement replace through the shared interface without an out-of-band channel or journaling events that QA's validator rejects; (2) the tighten-only rule (_check_replacement, order_event.py:440-446) can only be evaluated on the REPLACED event the adapter emits afterwards, i.e. after the simulated broker has already moved the stop: not fail closed; (3) the entry's attached_stop_price ('Protective stop held by the (simulated) broker for the resulting position') creates no order with a client_order_id and ExecutionAdapter has no modify-position call, so how S06 tightens Position.stop_price is undefined; 06 and 07 would diverge.
findings.proposed_change: While LOCK.json is PROPOSED, add to OrderEvent 1.0.0 the optional fields requested_volume_lots, requested_limit_price, requested_trigger_price, requested_valid_until_ns (invariant: only on REPLACE_REQUESTED, at least one set). In validate_order_transition run _check_replacement against the requested values on REPLACE_REQUESTED (so growth/widening is refused before the adapter is called; also call it in GuardedExecutionAdapter.replace, which should receive the previous event) and require on REPLACED that the current values equal the previous event's requested values. Define one protection path in SHARED_CONTRACTS sections 9/10: on fill the simulated broker materialises the attached stop as a PROTECTIVE_STOP order with client_order_id(run, position_id, 'PROTECTIVE_STOP', 0), and Position.stop_price mirrors that order's trigger.

findings.area: validate_order_transition / RECONCILED / G04-09, G04-10, G04-11, G08 restart reconciliation
findings.title: RECONCILED events are exempt from every no-added-risk rule
findings.detail: SHARED_CONTRACTS section 9: 'No replacement can add risk: an order's volume never grows, and an entry order's prices and attached stop are fixed to what risk approved' and 'A protective stop order may only be tightened when replaced'. order_event.py:395 exempts RECONCILED from the replaceable-field check and line 415 applies _check_replacement to REPLACED only. All of the following pass validate_order_transition (rt3.py T1, T7, T10): WORKING ENTRY 0.50 lots -> RECONCILED with volume_lots 50, limit 2649.80 -> 2655.00, attached stop 2647.80 -> 100, valid_until_ns -> null; WORKING protective SELL STOP 2647.80 -> RECONCILED trigger 2600 (control T6: the same change as REPLACED is refused with 'a protective stop may only be tightened, never widened'); RECONCILED turns the protective STOP into a SELL LIMIT at 9000. order_event.py:105-107 also lets RECONCILED move any non-terminal state to any state except PENDING_SUBMIT. MASTER G08: 'restart reconciliation, disconnect/stale-feed fail closed'.
findings.proposed_change: Apply _check_replacement to RECONCILED as well (volume not up, order_type fixed, ENTRY prices / attached stop / expiry fixed, protective trigger only tighter). If the simulated broker's state really differs in a risk-adding direction, treat it as a fault: raise/journal a GieError (e.g. reason RECONCILE_DIVERGENCE) and require a risk-reducing follow-up instead of adopting it as valid history. Restrict RECONCILED target states to those reachable without a pending request (WORKING, PARTIALLY_FILLED, FILLED, CANCELED, EXPIRED, REJECTED).

findings.area: RoutingGuard / GuardedExecutionAdapter (routing lock layer 3) / ExecutionAdapter Protocol
findings.title: The guard layer is bypassed without editing the lock module or the registry
findings.detail: SHARED_CONTRACTS section 9: 'An execution adapter is only reachable through the routing guard | GuardedExecutionAdapter'; section 10: 'An execution engine never holds a raw ExecutionAdapter'. Demonstrated with inert stand-ins (rt1.py, rt4.py): (a) guarded.py:31 accepts any isinstance(guard, RoutingGuard): 'class NoGuard(RoutingGuard): def authorize(self, adapter): return None' -> GuardedExecutionAdapter(Unregistered(), NoGuard('PAPER')).submit(req) reaches an unregistered adapter; (b) routing_lock.py:136-146 re-checks only venue and sends_real_orders on the instance: 'inst = HonestSim(); g = GuardedExecutionAdapter(inst, guard); inst.submit = other' -> g.submit(req) calls other; (c) 'HonestSim.submit = other' after registration (class-level patch) likewise; (d) 'obj.__class__ = HonestSim' on a foreign object passes the exact-type lookup; (e) g._adapter.submit(x) (guarded.py:28) calls the raw adapter with no authorisation and no request check, and the code that built the wrapper keeps its raw reference anyway. Also isinstance(GuardedExecutionAdapter(...), ExecutionAdapter) is False (no sends_real_orders) while a raw adapter is True, so an engine typed against the documented interface can only take the raw adapter. Prevented today: subclass of a registered type, instance override of the two declarations, look-alike venue enums, __class__ property spoof.
findings.proposed_change: (1) Make RoutingGuard final: __slots__ = ('_mode',), __init_subclass__ raises; in guarded.py require 'type(guard) is RoutingGuard' and call RoutingGuard.authorize(guard, adapter) unbound. (2) In register_simulated_adapter require the class to define __slots__ (instances without __dict__) and snapshot the six protocol functions; in authorize verify 'not hasattr(adapter, "__dict__")' and 'getattr(type(adapter), name) is snapshot[name]'. (3) Add GuardedExecutionAdapter.create(adapter_type, guard, **kwargs) that instantiates the adapter itself so no raw reference escapes. (4) Add an OrderGateway Protocol (the wrapper's surface) to interfaces.py for engines to depend on, and type the adapter declarations as Literal[ExecutionVenue.SIMULATED] and Literal[False].

findings.area: routing_lock.register_simulated_adapter / _SIMULATED_ADAPTER_TYPES
findings.title: Admission to the adapter registry is self-service: any class that declares itself simulated is authorised
findings.detail: routing_lock.py:84-102 admits any class whose two class attributes have the right values; who registers, from which module and when is unrestricted, and the registry is a plain module global (line 77). Reproduced (rt1.py A, H): '@register_simulated_adapter class LyingAdapter: venue = ExecutionVenue.SIMULATED; sends_real_orders = False; def submit(self, request): <any I/O>' is authorised by RoutingGuard('PAPER') and reached through GuardedExecutionAdapter.submit; 'routing_lock._SIMULATED_ADAPTER_TYPES.add(Smuggled)' followed by guard.authorize(Smuggled()) also succeeds. The module docstring (lines 15-18) presents registration as the admission control, but the declaration is asserted by the class being admitted. Classification: unmitigated at runtime; detectable only by the scan that does not exist (finding 1). MASTER G08: 'simulated adapter and live lock'.
findings.proposed_change: Smallest structural step: register_simulated_adapter refuses classes whose __module__ is not under a frozen allow-list (for example ('gie.execution.simulated', 'tests.')), and add seal_adapter_registry() (called implicitly by the first RoutingGuard.__init__) after which registration raises LiveRoutingLockedError. Scan rule: the import closure of an allow-listed adapter module contains no network, process, ctypes or broker module.

findings.area: OrderEvent OEV-6 / OrderIntent / G04 (no averaging down, hard protective stops)
findings.title: Orders that are not ENTRY can create or increase exposure with no plan and no risk approval, and protection can be shrunk or cancelled
findings.detail: order_event.py:27-28 states 'Only ENTRY creates risk and needs a risk approval' as an assumption; OEV-6 (lines 292-303) only requires a position_id. Accepted records (rt3.py O6, O7, T8, T9; rt6.py E2): intent=EXIT, side=BUY, volume_lots=50 against the sample LONG 0.50-lot position (same side, 100 times the size, no plan, no RiskDecision); intent=PROTECTIVE_STOP with order_type=MARKET; an EXIT addressed to identity.external_position_id('fixture-account','FIXTURE-TICKET-1'), i.e. another system's position (position.py:20-22: GIE 'never manages them'); a protective stop REPLACED from 0.50 to 0.01 lots (0.49 lots left unprotected, validate_order_transition passes because only growth is refused, order_event.py:432); a protective stop CANCEL_REQUESTED -> CANCELED while the position is open (section 9: 'A stop is never wider than the initial stop and never removed'). MASTER G04: 'no martingale, averaging down or widening protective stops. Hard protective stops'.
findings.proposed_change: Add gie.contracts validate_reducing_order(position, request): owner is GIE, same run, request.side opposite to position.side, volume_lots <= position.volume_lots, PROTECTIVE_STOP is a STOP order on the losing side of the mark, TAKE_PROFIT is a LIMIT order; make GuardedExecutionAdapter.submit require the Position for non-ENTRY intents and call it. Add the intent/order-type pairing as an OrderEvent invariant. In _check_replacement forbid reducing a PROTECTIVE_STOP's volume below the open volume, and state in section 9 when a protective stop may be cancelled (only together with a tighter replacement or after the position is CLOSED).

findings.area: OEV-5 / RiskDecision binding / identity.plan_id, identity.client_order_id / GuardedExecutionAdapter.submit
findings.title: An entry order's link to its plan and approval is referential only; one approval can be spent several times and for any size
findings.detail: SHARED_CONTRACTS section 9: 'Every entry order carries its plan, its risk approval and an attached protective stop' and 'an approval is bound to one plan, reserves risk and expires'. OEV-5 (order_event.py:280-291) checks only that three fields are non-null. Accepted (rt3.py O4, O5, P5; rt6.py E1, E7, E8): ENTRY with volume_lots 500 citing a decision that granted 0.50; ENTRY citing the id of a REJECTED decision; two ENTRY orders with client_order_id attempt 0 and 1 both citing the same decision/reservation (1.00 lots on a 0.50-lot approval; 'attempt' is not a field, identity.py:72-79, so the id is not verifiable); an approval dated one hour before its plan and outliving it by ten years. Nothing compares attached_stop_price with the plan's stop_price. plan_id = f(candidate, entry_style, variant, revision) (identity.py:60-61) does not cover the geometry: samples.trade_plan().plan_id == samples.trade_plan(stop_price=Decimal('2600')).plan_id, so 'what risk approved' is not pinned by the approval. No shared function checks plan/decision/order together and GuardedExecutionAdapter.submit (guarded.py:69-70) receives only the OrderEvent. Brief 07 acceptance: 'stale plans, no real orders'; brief 08: 'simultaneous reservations atomic'.
findings.proposed_change: (1) Add validate_entry_authorization(plan, decision, request, now_ns) to gie.contracts: same run/mode, decision.approved, decision.plan_id == plan.plan_id == request.plan_id, same side, request.volume_lots <= decision.volume_lots, request.attached_stop_price == plan.stop_price, order price == plan.entry_price, now_ns < min(plan.valid_until_ns, decision.valid_until_ns), decision.decision_time_ns >= plan.decision_time_ns; GuardedExecutionAdapter.submit(request, *, plan, decision, now_ns) calls it for ENTRY. (2) Make one approval = one order structural: ENTRY client_order_id = identity.client_order_id(run_id, risk_decision_id, 'ENTRY', 0), verified by a new invariant (all parts are fields). (3) Put side, entry price and stop_price (or a plan fingerprint) into RiskDecision.

findings.area: routing_lock.assert_live_routing_locked / parse_run_mode / _spec.EnumOf.check (routing lock layer 1)
findings.title: The vocabulary self-check misses alias names and injected members; a LIVE mode then passes the guard and LIVE records can be built
findings.detail: SHARED_CONTRACTS section 9 row 1: 'No live mode or real venue exists in the vocabulary'; routing_lock.py:10-12: 'a live order event cannot even be constructed or decoded'. (a) routing_lock.py:70-73 compares only the values obtained by iterating the enum, so a LIVE name that aliases PAPER is invisible; the repository's own test tests/gie/core/test_routing_lock.py::test_the_self_check_raises_when_a_vocabulary_gains_a_live_name_as_an_alias fails for both vocabularies ('DID NOT RAISE'). (b) rt2.py: a member added to RunMode._member_map_ and _value2member_map_ (not _member_names_) is equally invisible; afterwards assert_live_routing_locked() returns normally, parse_run_mode(RunMode('LIVE')) returns it (line 54 is an isinstance test), RoutingGuard(live).mode is LIVE, samples.order_event(mode=live, venue=live_venue) and samples.risk_decision(mode=live) construct (EnumOf.check, _spec.py:364-371, is isinstance) and to_wire emits mode LIVE / venue LIVE, and a LIVE-mode request passes GuardedExecutionAdapter when the guard was built with that mode. 'RunMode.LIVE = RunMode.PAPER' (plain attribute) is also silent. Still safe: decoding (EnumOf._by_value is an import-time snapshot) and the venue check in guarded.py:48 (identity). Requires deliberate tampering, so detect-only today.
findings.proposed_change: Capture the members at import (_RUN_MODES = (RunMode.REPLAY, RunMode.PAPER); _VENUES = (ExecutionVenue.SIMULATED,)). Self-check: dict(RunMode.__members__) must map exactly REPLAY and PAPER to those captured objects (identity), set(RunMode._value2member_map_) == {'REPLAY','PAPER'}, 'LIVE' not in vars(RunMode); same for the venue. parse_run_mode: return only when 'value is' a captured member (or the exact strings). EnumOf.check: require self._by_value.get(getattr(value, 'value', None)) is value.

findings.area: gie/contracts/_spec.py Record, Obj.check / guarded._check_event / codec.to_wire / COM-06
findings.title: An unvalidated subclass of a contract passes every isinstance check, encodes as the contract and is accepted by GuardedExecutionAdapter
findings.detail: SHARED_CONTRACTS section 5 rule 2: 'Every record that exists in memory is valid: validation runs on construction and on decoding'; section 1: 'A subsystem MUST NOT redefine, copy or locally extend a shared contract (COM-06)' is stated but not enforced. Reproduced (rt4.py U1): '@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True, kw_only=True) class EvilOrderEvent(OrderEvent): def __post_init__(self): pass' constructs with symbol 'EURUSD', volume_lots -1, no attached stop, no plan, no risk decision; isinstance(evil, OrderEvent) is True, type(evil).CONTRACT == 'OrderEvent', to_wire(evil) emits it as an OrderEvent, and GuardedExecutionAdapter(Sim(), RoutingGuard('PAPER')).submit(evil) hands it to the adapter (guarded.py:46 uses isinstance; Obj.check at _spec.py:500-507 likewise). With a look-alike venue enum the same subclass serialises as contract OrderEvent with venue LIVE (the wrapper's identity check on venue does refuse that one). rt6.py E4: object.__setattr__(record, 'symbol', 'EURUSD') mutates a validated record and to_wire emits it (not preventable in Python; scan item).
findings.proposed_change: Record.__init_subclass__ raises TypeError unless cls.__module__ starts with 'gie.contracts.'; use exact-type checks (type(event) is OrderEvent) in guarded.py, Obj.check and in to_wire (get_contract(t.CONTRACT) is t); mark the nine contract classes @final. Add the object.__setattr__ rule to the scan (finding 1).

findings.area: TradePlan PLN-5 / OrderEvent OEV-9 / Position POS-4 / G04-12
findings.title: 'Stop on the losing side' is vacuous for market entries and is never related to the executable price or the fill
findings.detail: SHARED_CONTRACTS section 9: 'Every plan has a hard stop on the losing side and targets on the winning side | PLN-5, PLN-6'; OEV-9: 'attached protection is on the correct side of the order price'. (a) order_event.py:134-137: _protection_geometry returns True when the order has no price, so OEV-9 checks nothing for any MARKET entry. Accepted (rt3.py O1, O2): BUY MARKET ENTRY with attached_stop_price 9999 and take profit 1; its FILLED event (average_fill_price 2650.35, 'protective' stop 9999) passes validate_order_transition. (b) PLN-5 compares the stop with entry_price only (trade_plan.py:93-99), not with reference_price: BUY LIMIT entry 2700 while the ask is 2650.35 (marketable) with stop 2660 is accepted (P1): the stop lies above the price at which the order fills. (c) POS-4 (position.py:56-61) never relates the initial stop to the entry: GIE BUY position, entry 2649.80, initial_stop_price 9000 accepted (rt4.py S1). (d) no minimum distance: a stop 1E-12 below the entry gives risk_per_unit 1E-12 (P2); a stop at 0.000000000001 is accepted (P3). MASTER G04: 'Hard protective stops'.
findings.proposed_change: OEV-9: when average_fill_price is set, attached stop and take profit must be on the correct side of it; add reference_price to OrderEvent (mandatory for MARKET ENTRY) and check against it on SUBMIT_REQUESTED. TradePlan: BUY LIMIT entry <= reference, BUY STOP entry >= reference (mirrored for SELL), stop and targets on the correct side of both entry and reference. Position: BUY initial_stop_price < average_entry_price (SELL >). Minimum stop distance, tick size, volume step and maximum volume are broker data: an InstrumentSpec shared contract is REQUIRED before S07/S08 can validate geometry and size (CR-003 / U-10 are open); say this in section 9 instead of presenting the hard stop as fully structural.

findings.area: RiskDecision RSK-3, RSK-7 / G05-07, G05-08 / brief 08 acceptance
findings.title: An approval a hair above the profit floor may risk far more than the surplus; risk_frac may be 0 or 500 %
findings.detail: MASTER G05: 'Above +5% protect a nondecreasing daily profit floor, exceptional setups only with surplus risk budget after costs and open exposure. At exactly the floor no new risk.' RSK-7 (risk_decision.py:170-178) only tests daily_pnl_frac > profit_floor_frac. Accepted (rt4.py R4): PROFIT_PROTECTION, daily_pnl_frac 0.0500000001, profit_floor_frac 0.05, APPROVED with risk_frac 0.02: the loss at the stop ends about 2 % of equity below the protected floor although the surplus was 1E-10 (control R5: exactly at the floor is refused). Also accepted: APPROVED with risk_frac 0 and risk_amount 1E15 (RSK-3, lines 142-154, does not require risk_frac > 0 although section 2 names risk_frac as the field used in limit comparisons); risk_frac 5; profit_floor_frac -0.9 in PROFIT_PROTECTION; quality_validated=True with nothing to verify it against. The record carries neither the day's reference equity nor open/pending risk as fractions, so no fraction is recomputable, and there is no validator that the floor is non-decreasing within a trading_day.
findings.proposed_change: RSK-3: an approval requires risk_frac > 0 and risk_frac <= 1. New RSK-10: in PROFIT_PROTECTION an approval requires risk_frac <= daily_pnl_frac - profit_floor_frac (EXACT arithmetic), ideally less open and pending risk fractions. Add reference_equity_amount (and open_risk_frac, pending_risk_frac) so that risk_amount == risk_frac * reference_equity_amount can be asserted. Add validate_daily_state_sequence(previous, next) (same trading_day: floor non-decreasing, times monotone). An AccountSnapshot shared contract (reference equity, day P&L, floor, state, exposure of other systems) is REQUIRED before S08 can emit auditable RiskDecisions.

findings.area: Position POS-2 / validate_position_transition / PositionOwner.EXTERNAL / G05 'including other positions'
findings.title: GIE's own monotonic rules are applied to other systems' positions, so truthful observations are refused
findings.detail: MASTER G05: 'Track Prague day and actual account rules, including other positions'; brief 08 acceptance: 'other-account-position handling'; MASTER: 'never ... invent data'. position.py:17-23: EXTERNAL positions are observed, never managed. Yet POS-2 (lines 163-167) and validate_position_transition (lines 263-270) apply to every owner. Refused although true (rt4.py S4-S6): an external SELL position whose owner widens its stop 1.0900 -> 1.0950 ('the protective stop may not be widened or removed'); the owner removes its stop; a netting position that grows 0.50 -> 1.00 lots (POS-2 fails at construction). SHARED_CONTRACTS section 5 rule 6 then says 'the offending record MUST NOT be journaled as valid history', so S07/S08 must either drop the observation (account-wide risk is understated exactly when another system increases risk) or fabricate a different record. Related: a GIE position_id is not verified although run_id and opening_client_order_id are fields (section 4 promises self-verification; 'pos_' + 32 zeros is accepted, S2), so a second rev-0 GIE position for the same plan with a 650-USD-wide stop passes (S8).
findings.proposed_change: Apply the volume, stop and peak monotonicity only when owner is PositionOwner.GIE; for EXTERNAL keep the identity immutables and time monotonicity and drop POS-2 (or define initial_volume_lots as the largest observed volume). Add invariant POS-8: for owner GIE, position_id == identity.position_id(run_id, opening_client_order_id).

findings.area: OrderEvent.valid_until_ns / RSK-8 / section 3.3 freshness / G03-12 / brief 07 'stale plans'
findings.title: Entry orders may have no expiry, may be submitted already expired and may have their expiry removed by a replacement
findings.detail: SHARED_CONTRACTS section 3.3: 'A stale or expired input MUST NOT lead to an action that creates or increases risk'; RiskDecision docstring: 'execution must not act on an expired approval'; MASTER G03: 'reject stale signals'. OrderEvent.valid_until_ns is 'null for no expiry' for every intent. Accepted (rt3.py O3, T3; rt6.py E3; rt4.py R3): ENTRY LIMIT with valid_until_ns=None although the sample approval lives 30 s and the plan 120 s (the resting order can fill hours later on an expired approval); ENTRY with valid_until_ns one hour before its own event_time_ns; a REPLACED event that changes an ENTRY's expiry from T0+120 s to null (order_event.py:426-428 explicitly lets the expiry change in either direction); an approval valid until 2^63-1 (RSK-8 only requires > decision_time_ns).
findings.proposed_change: New OrderEvent invariant: a LIMIT or STOP ENTRY has valid_until_ns set, and on SUBMIT_REQUESTED it is later than event_time_ns. _check_replacement: an ENTRY's valid_until_ns may only decrease. validate_entry_authorization (see the entry-authorisation finding): request.valid_until_ns <= min(plan.valid_until_ns, decision.valid_until_ns). State in section 3.3 that the simulated broker must expire an entry at that instant and that a fill after the approval's expiry is a contract violation.

findings.area: ModelVersion / tests/gie/samples.py / COM-07 fixture labelling / RiskDecision.quality_validated
findings.title: ModelVersion carries no origin or fixture label: the fixture ACTIVE model with a made-up owner approval is indistinguishable from a real one
findings.detail: Brief 00: 'If a dependency is unavailable, use explicitly labeled test fixtures only'; CLAUDE.md rule 4. SHARED_CONTRACTS section 9 last row: 'Every record names its run, mode and the origin of its data (fixtures are labelled) | RunScoped header, Tick.origin'. model_version.py:89 'class ModelVersion(Sequenced)' has no run_id, mode or data_origin. tests/gie/samples.py:501-515 builds an ACTIVE version with approved_by='FIXTURE-OWNER' and approval_reference='D-999'; its wire form is status ACTIVE, approved_by FIXTURE-OWNER, approval_reference D-999, model_name fixture_net_r: the only markers are free-text values, and .validated (model_version.py:208-211) is True. tools/make_golden.py will write it to tests/gie/golden/ModelVersion-1.0.0/active.json. approval_reference only has to match ^D-[0-9]{3,5}$ and approved_by accepts a single space (rt4.py M1). RiskDecision.quality_validated ('True only when the size was adapted using quality from an owner-approved (ACTIVE) model version') names no model, so it cannot be checked against the registry. MASTER G04: 'Adaptive sizing only from validated quality'; G07: 'versioned promotion with owner approval'.
findings.proposed_change: Add training_data_origin: DataOrigin to ModelVersion with the invariant 'ACTIVE requires training_data_origin != SYNTHETIC_FIXTURE'; reserve an approval-reference range for fixtures that a registry refuses outside tests, and let the register tooling check that every ACTIVE record cites an existing APPROVED decision in docs/DECISION_LOG.md; give approved_by a non-blank pattern; add quality_model_version_id to RiskDecision (set if and only if quality_validated).

findings.area: ModelVersion MDL-2, MDL-5, MDL-6 / MODEL_STATUS_TRANSITIONS / G07-09, G07-10, G07-11
findings.title: 'ACTIVE only after SHADOW' is not structural; any retired model can be re-activated on its old approval; the first active model cannot be rolled back
findings.detail: SHARED_CONTRACTS section 9: 'A model can be ACTIVE only after SHADOW and only with a recorded owner approval; rollback re-activates the retired parent, again only with a recorded approval', under 'a record that violates them cannot be constructed or decoded'. (a) rt4.py M1: samples.model_version(revision=1, seq=1, status=ModelStatus.ACTIVE, approved_by=' ', approval_reference='D-000') constructs and .validated is True; revision 1 cannot have been preceded by RESEARCH and SHADOW, but only MDL-5 (revision 0 is RESEARCH, model_version.py:196-200) is an invariant. (b) M2: RESEARCH -> SHADOW -> ACTIVE(D-999) -> RETIRED -> ACTIVE(D-999) passes validate_model_transition: the table (line 68) lets any RETIRED version return to ACTIVE, with the same approval reference and without any rolled-back successor. (c) M3: the first ACTIVE version has no parent, so ACTIVE -> ROLLED_BACK is refused by MDL-6; MASTER G07: 'versioned promotion with owner approval and rollback'. (d) ModelRegistry.get/active (interfaces.py:94-104) return records without any obligation that validate_model_transition was applied.
findings.proposed_change: New invariant: SHADOW requires revision >= 1 and ACTIVE requires revision >= 2. Add rollback_of_model_version_id: a RETIRED -> ACTIVE entry must name the ROLLED_BACK successor and carry an approval_reference different from the version's previous activation (give the validator the last ACTIVE revision to compare). Decide and document rollback for a version without parent (allow ROLLED_BACK with parent null meaning 'no active model: unscored, fail closed').

findings.area: SHARED_CONTRACTS section 9 wording / validate_*_transition / RecordSink / tests
findings.title: Seven of the seventeen 'structural' safety rules hold only if a caller remembers to invoke a validator, and nothing forces or tests that
findings.detail: Section 9 opens: 'These are structural: a record that violates them cannot be constructed or decoded.' The rows 'A stop is never wider than the initial stop and never removed', 'A protective stop order may only be tightened when replaced', 'No replacement can add risk', 'An execution adapter is only reachable through the routing guard', 'A position is never increased', 'The executable net P&L peak never decreases' and 'A model can be ACTIVE only after SHADOW' cite validate_position_transition, validate_order_transition, MODEL_STATUS_TRANSITIONS or GuardedExecutionAdapter; each offending record constructs and decodes on its own (for example a Position revision whose stop is wider than the previous revision's but not wider than the initial stop). interfaces.py:35-44: RecordSink.publish promises only idempotence per (stream, seq); nothing in gie.core or gie.contracts keeps the previous event per order, position or model. No test references GuardedExecutionAdapter or any validate_*_transition (grep over tests/ and tools/ finds nothing; tests/gie/contracts/ does not exist). Sessions 07, 09, 11 and 12 would each decide where, or whether, to call them. SHARED_CONTRACTS section 5 rule 6: 'the offending record MUST NOT be journaled as valid history'.
findings.proposed_change: Split section 9 into 'record invariants (cannot be constructed)' and 'sequence rules (validators; mandatory call sites)'. Add gie.contracts.ledger.LifecycleLedger that keeps the newest OrderEvent per client_order_id, Position per position_id and ModelVersion per model_version_id and whose admit(record) calls the matching validator and raises before publication; require in section 10 that every RecordSink for these three contracts is fed through it. Add tests/gie/contracts/test_transitions.py and test_guarded_adapter.py (the latter is already named in acceptance_tests.yaml AT-S00-ACC-04).

findings.area: gie/core/params.py / specifications/research_parameters.toml / G05 thresholds, M-DIR-08
findings.title: The research-parameter loader fails open on unit, sign, ordering and omission errors and accepts non-canonical decimals
findings.detail: MASTER: 'Proposed numerical settings are research parameters, not approved production limits'; G05: 'defensive at -2% ... emergency halt at -3%'; brief 08: 'Boundary tests at -2%, proposed -1.75%, -3%, +5%'. params.py:89-129 says it 'fails closed on any defect' but validates only shape. Loaded without error from modified copies (rt5.py Q1-Q11): daily_emergency_halt_threshold_frac = '-3' (percent typed instead of a fraction: halt at -300 %, i.e. never), '0.03' (wrong sign), '-0.01' (above the defensive level); the profit-protection table deleted entirely; value '0_5' -> Decimal 5, ' 5 ' -> 5, '1e3' -> 1E+3 (Decimal(raw) at line 76 accepts underscores, whitespace and exponents, not the wire grammar of section 7); tick target -5 or '0.001'; unknown top-level key approved_by_owner = true and per-parameter key approved_limit = true silently ignored; schema_version = true and 1.0 accepted (line 99 compares '!= 1'; the repository's own tests test_schema_version_of_the_wrong_type_is_refused[bool] and [float] fail). Working as intended: any approval_status other than PROPOSED_RESEARCH_PARAMETERS is refused, floats are refused. value() returns a bare number and no record states which parameter set it was decided under.
findings.proposed_change: Parse decimals with gie.core.canonical.decimal_from_str; require type(schema_version) is int; reject unknown keys at both levels; declare in params.py the required names with type and range (*_ns: int > 0; *_frac: Decimal with abs < 1) and the order halt < defensive < recovery < 0 < profit_protection, raising ConfigError otherwise; expose parameters_sha256 and require it in the run configuration hash (identity.run_id's docstring already says the hash 'must cover ... parameters').

findings.area: README.md / docs/CHANGE_REQUESTS.md B-001 / docs/ARCHITECTURE.md / M-AUTH-08 'never mark placeholders complete'
findings.title: Documents state deliverables as done that are not in the tree
findings.detail: MASTER: 'never silently simplify, invent data, or mark placeholders complete'; owner directive: 'Do not ... declare incomplete components finished'. At HEAD 91e004b: README.md:3-6 'nothing in this repository can send an order to a broker' and 'Session 00 (foundation) submitted for owner review', pointing to reviews/session_00/ (empty) and specifications/REQUIREMENTS_MATRIX.md (absent); docs/CHANGE_REQUESTS.md:32-35 'not performed; tool delivered' (tools/audit/ does not exist), 'harness built and self-tested on a labelled synthetic fixture' (tools/baseline_freeze.py absent), 'proven for this repository (protected path check)' (tools/check_protected_paths.py absent); ARCHITECTURE.md:72-73, 104-110, 129-133 and D-006, D-011, D-015 describe check_architecture, check_live_lock and gie_registers as existing; CLAUDE.md lists docs/IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md (absent). The registers are honest (requirements_matrix.yaml S00-ACC-04..06 'not_started', acceptance_tests.yaml 91 x 'planned') and the commits are marked WIP, so this is a snapshot defect, but these are the sentences a review package would quote. Verified true: git hash-object Start = ff972e3e86e8628ee696ede5ca1a3c8f92fe1197, equal to protected_paths in dependency_graph.yaml; no credential-like strings found.
findings.proposed_change: Before the gate either deliver the five tools, the audit tool and the review package, or reword each sentence to its true state ('planned', 'not yet implemented'). Add a CI step that fails when a path named in README.md, CLAUDE.md, ARCHITECTURE.md or CHANGE_REQUESTS.md does not exist, and let tools/build_review.py refuse to build while it fails. Replace 'nothing in this repository can send an order' by the checkable statement 'no module under gie/ imports a network or broker library (tools/check_live_lock)'.

findings.area: gie/core/canonical.py, gie/contracts/_spec.py, codec.py, registry.py, errors.py / SHARED_CONTRACTS section 5 rule 2
findings.title: Five places where invalid input is defaulted, stripped or rounded, or where a non-GIE error escapes
findings.detail: Section 5.2: 'Invalid input ... is never clamped, defaulted, rounded or coerced.' (a) _spec.py:658-662: an OrderEvent message of version 1.0.0 with the key valid_until_ns removed decodes and the field becomes None, i.e. 'no expiry' (rt4.py C1); section 7 says writers always write optional fields as explicit null, so a missing key in a same-version message is corruption, and here the default is the risk-increasing value. (b) canonical.py:79, registry.py:30 and ids.py:98 use re.match with '$', which also matches before a trailing newline: a limit_price string with a trailing newline decodes to Decimal('2649.80') and a schema_version with a trailing newline is accepted (C2, C3; failing tests test_decimal_from_str_rejects_a_trailing_newline, test_is_valid_id_rejects_a_trailing_newline). (c) _spec.py:285-302: Float.check accepts ints and rounds silently on construction: NamedValue(name='abc', value=2**53+1).value == 9007199254740992.0, while decoding the same value is refused ('integer is not exactly representable as a double'). (d) samples.tick(bid=Decimal('1E+1000000')) raises a raw decimal.Overflow, not a GieError (section 5: 'All errors derive from gie.core.errors.GieError'). (e) GieError.details accepts integers beyond 64 bits that canonical JSON cannot journal (failing tests test_errors_for_integers_beyond_64_bits_can_be_journaled). In my run on the copy 34 of 1,955 tests failed.
findings.proposed_change: Use re.fullmatch in decimal_from_str, parse_semver, is_valid_id and the timeutil patterns. Give FieldSpec a 'since' version and treat a missing key as ContractValidationError for every field with since <= message version. Float.check: accept float, and int only when float(v) == v. Catch decimal.DecimalException in decimal_to_str / Dec.check and raise CanonicalEncodingError. Validate details values in GieError.__init__ (int64 range, finite floats).

findings.area: gie/contracts/compat.py / schema_gen.py / schemas/LOCK.json
findings.title: The schema evolution check treats adding a LIVE venue or mode as a MINOR change, and the PROPOSED lock allows it in place
findings.detail: routing_lock.py:22-24: unlocking 'would need a code change to this module, a new major version of the OrderEvent contract and a recorded owner approval'. compat.py:82-88 classifies any added enum value as MINOR. rt5.py: appending 'LIVE' to properties.venue.enum and properties.mode.enum of OrderEvent-1.0.0.schema.json gives classify_schema_change = MINOR and check_evolution('1.0.0' -> '1.1.0') returns no problem. LOCK.json approval_status is PROPOSED, and schema_gen.write (lines 151-177) rewrites a locked 1.0.0 schema in place in that state, so not even the bump is needed. The schema lock therefore does not back up layer 1; only assert_live_routing_locked and the tests do.
findings.proposed_change: In schema_gen.check(), independent of the lock status, assert for every contract schema that sorted(properties.mode.enum) == ['PAPER','REPLAY'] and, where present, properties.venue.enum == ['SIMULATED']. In compat, report any change of those two enums as MAJOR plus an explicit problem 'routing-lock vocabulary changed'.

findings.area: gie/core/freshness.py / SHARED_CONTRACTS section 3.3 / look-ahead (G10, S10-ACC-02)
findings.title: 'Future tolerance MUST be 0 in replay' cannot be enforced by the freshness helpers
findings.detail: Section 3.3: 'A tolerance for cross-host skew exists for paper mode and MUST be 0 in replay.' freshness.py:27-47 takes future_tolerance_ns from the caller and knows neither the clock nor the mode. rt5.py F1: is_fresh(now_ns=1_000_000_000, reference_ns=6_000_000_000, max_age_ns=10, future_tolerance_ns=10_000_000_000) returns True: data five seconds in the future counts as fresh, with its age clamped to 0 at line 47. In a replay this is look-ahead that is accepted without any record of it.
findings.proposed_change: Let the helpers take the injected Clock (clock.now_ns(), clock.mode) instead of now_ns and raise ContractValidationError when clock.mode is ClockMode.REPLAY and future_tolerance_ns != 0; make the tolerance a bounded research parameter.

findings.area: DataOrigin / Tick.receive_time_ns / RunScoped header / identity.run_id / M-AUTH-07, G09-10
findings.title: Modelled receive times are not flagged, and origin and run labels are self-declared
findings.detail: MASTER: 'never ... invent data'; G09: 'Use actual tick data for fast execution claims.' (a) tick.py:66-71: for imported history without a recorded receive time, receive_time_ns 'equals event_time_ns plus the modelled feed delay': an invented value inside a record labelled HISTORICAL, with no flag; delays computed as decision_time_ns - as_of_time_ns then look measured. (b) data_origin on derived records is set by the producer; combine_origins (common.py:105-109) is optional, so evidence built on SYNTHETIC_FIXTURE ticks can be emitted as BROKER_FEED and no rule ties a PAPER run to non-fixture origins. (c) identity.run_id(mode, config_sha256, label) (identity.py:20-26) accepts any strings, including mode 'LIVE', and a record's mode field is not tied to the mode inside its run_id.
findings.proposed_change: Add TickFlag RECEIVE_TIME_MODELLED (mandatory when the receive time was not recorded) and exclude such ticks from latency evidence. Provide derive_origin(*inputs) and let the ledger/QA check that a record's origin is not more trustworthy than its inputs. Validate run_id arguments (mode through parse_run_mode, config hash by the SHA-256 pattern) and add a run manifest record binding run_id to mode, configuration hash, parameter hash and code commit.

findings.area: routing lock scope / session 01 market data and account observation / credentials (beyond the specification)
findings.title: A broker data connection normally shares its API and login with order entry; decide read-only credentials and a single facade now
findings.detail: Suggestion beyond the spec; the existing system could not be inspected (B-001), so the real interface is unknown. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:104-106 foresees broker SDK imports for 'read-only market data', PAPER mode needs live quotes, and G05 requires observing other systems' positions on the real account. Terminal APIs of the MetaTrader kind expose order entry on the same module and logged-in session as quotes and account state, so a process logged in with trading rights is one call away from a real order regardless of RoutingGuard; the lock in this repository cannot see that. MASTER: 'keep real order routing disabled. Do not expose credentials.'; owner directive: 'Preserve all existing trading systems.'
findings.proposed_change: Record an open item for the owner: the PAPER data and account-observation connection uses read-only (investor) credentials or an account with trading disabled, supplied outside the repository; one facade module re-exports only read functions and is the only place allowed to import the SDK; the scan forbids the SDK's order-entry names everywhere and forbids subprocess calls or file writes towards D:\ftmo_eurusd so the existing bots cannot be driven indirectly.

findings.area: identity.external_position_id / Position.external_ref / evidence files (beyond the specification)
findings.title: The external position id can reveal the broker account number, and free-text fields have no pattern that keeps secrets out
findings.detail: Suggestion beyond the spec. MASTER: 'Do not expose credentials.' identity.py:95-97 hashes account_ref together with the broker ticket, and Position.external_ref ('Broker ticket', free text up to 64 characters, position.py:91-94) is journaled next to the id. If account_ref is the broker login number (8 to 10 digits) it can be recovered from any journal or evidence file by brute force over the truncated SHA-256 with the known ticket. A login number is not a secret on its own, but it is half of the terminal credentials and identifies the owner's account in files uploaded as review evidence. external_ref, approved_by and GieError.details accept arbitrary printable text.
findings.proposed_change: Document that account_ref MUST be a locally configured alias, never the login; give external_ref a pattern such as ^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,64}$; add a secret-pattern scan over reviews/ and CI evidence files.

findings.area: S00-ASG-25 event ordering / gie/core/ordering.py StreamRank, gie/contracts/ordering.py ordering_key, SHARED_CONTRACTS 6.2
findings.title: The run total order is anti-causal when a decision chain shares one instant - which is always the case in replay
findings.detail:
SHARED_CONTRACTS.md 6.2 (l.228-236): "All records of a run are processed in ascending EventKey = (time_ns, rank, stream, seq)" with tie-break "clock, tick, order event, position, risk decision, evidence, candidate, trade plan, model version ... Execution facts therefore precede intelligence derived at the same instant." Section 1 (l.37) gives the data flow Tick -> Evidence -> Candidate -> TradePlan -> RiskDecision -> OrderEvent -> Position. Section 3.2: ReplayClock "moves only when the replay driver advances it", so in REPLAY every record derived from one tick carries the same decision/receive time and only rank decides. With StreamRank (gie/core/ordering.py:42-54) and ordering_key (gie/contracts/ordering.py:18-24, 43-61) the SUBMIT_REQUESTED order event sorts BEFORE the RiskDecision that approved it, which sorts BEFORE the TradePlan, Candidate and Evidence it came from.
Reproducer (cwd /home/user/Hello): python3 -B -c "from tests.gie import samples as S; from gie.contracts.ordering import ordering_key as k; t=S.T0; r={'tick':S.tick(receive_time_ns=t,event_time_ns=t),'evidence':S.evidence(decision_time_ns=t,as_of_time_ns=t),'candidate':S.candidate(decision_time_ns=t,as_of_time_ns=t),'plan':S.trade_plan(decision_time_ns=t,as_of_time_ns=t),'risk':S.risk_decision(decision_time_ns=t,as_of_time_ns=t),'order':S.order_event(event_time_ns=t,receive_time_ns=t),'position':S.position(decision_time_ns=t,as_of_time_ns=t,opened_time_ns=t)}; print(sorted(r,key=lambda n:k(r[n])))" -> ['tick', 'order', 'position', 'risk', 'evidence', 'candidate', 'plan'].
Consequences: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:121 defines the journal as "per stream", so every consumer that rebuilds a run with merge_ordered (09, 10, 11, 12) processes effects before causes (plan_id / risk_decision_id referenced before the record exists); REPLAY (equal instants) orders the same logical flow differently from PAPER (microseconds apart); and "Replay of the same inputs MUST reproduce the same sequence of records byte for byte" (l.239-241) becomes ambiguous between emission order and EventKey order, so sessions 07 and 10 can each be 'deterministic' and still disagree.
findings.proposed_change: Make the tie-break causal.
