Preferred: add a run-wide emission counter (e.g. run_seq, assigned by the run's RecordSink / composition root and persisted with the journal) and define the total order of GIE-produced records as (availability time, run_seq); keep StreamRank only for independent exogenous inputs that share an instant (clock, tick, recorded broker events). Minimum if no field is added: reorder the ranks of derived records to the data flow (EVIDENCE < CANDIDATE < TRADE_PLAN < RISK_DECISION < ORDER_EVENT < POSITION), state in 6.2 that rank orders only independent information, and add a test that in the sample pipeline every record's key is greater than the key of every record it references.

findings.area: Identity / RiskDecision <-> TradePlan <-> OrderEvent (RSK-3, OEV-5, SHARED_CONTRACTS section 9), G04
findings.title: A risk approval is bound to plan_id, but plan_id is not bound to the plan's content (entry, stop, targets)
findings.detail:
gie/contracts/identity.py:60-61: plan_id = make_id('pln', candidate, entry_style, variant, revision) - no price enters the identity. RiskDecision carries only `plan_id` (gie/contracts/risk_decision.py:54); OrderEvent ENTRY carries plan_id, risk_decision_id and attached_stop_price (OEV-5). SHARED_CONTRACTS section 9 claims "an approval is bound to one plan" (RSK-2/3/8) and "an entry order's prices and attached stop are fixed to what risk approved"; master G04: "no martingale, averaging down or widening protective stops. Hard protective stops". Nothing in the contracts lets execution or QA check that the stop on the order is the stop risk evaluated, because two different plans can legitimately carry the same plan_id and PLN-1 still holds.
Reproducer: python3 -B -c "from decimal import Decimal as D; from tests.gie import samples as S; a=S.trade_plan(); b=S.trade_plan(seq=1, stop_price=D('2600.00')); print(a.plan_id==b.plan_id, a.risk_per_unit, b.risk_per_unit, a==b)" -> True 2.00 49.80 False. Both records are accepted by SequenceTracker (different seq), and S.order_event(attached_stop_price=D('2600.00'), plan_id=b.plan_id, risk_decision_id=<approval of a>) constructs: an entry with 25x the approved stop distance under the approval given for plan a. validate_order_transition only fixes the order to its OWN first event, not to the approved plan.
findings.proposed_change: Bind the approval to content. Either (a) add `plan_fingerprint` (codec.fingerprint of the evaluated TradePlan) - or the approved entry_price/stop_price - to RiskDecision and add a shared validator, e.g. validate_entry_against_approval(plan, decision, submit_event), that 07 must call and 12 can run on journals; or (b) derive plan_id from the plan's risk-relevant content (side, entry, stop, targets) so that a changed plan is necessarily a new id and needs a new approval. Add a negative test with the reproducer above.

findings.area: Clock contract / gie/core/clock.py SystemClock, SHARED_CONTRACTS 3.2-3.3, G03-12, G08
findings.title: SystemClock clamp freezes now_ns: freshness and expiry fail OPEN for the whole length of a backward clock step, and the Clock protocol exposes no health
findings.detail:
gie/core/clock.py:266-273: while the OS wall clock is behind the last reading, now_ns() returns the previous value unchanged. SHARED_CONTRACTS 3.3 requires that freshness "fails closed at the boundary"; master G08: "disconnect/stale-feed fail closed"; G03: "reject stale signals". With a frozen now_ns every age stays 0 and no valid_until_ns is ever reached until real time has caught up (NTP step, manual correction, VM resume - seconds to hours).
Reproducer: python3 -B -c "from gie.core.clock import SystemClock; from gie.core import freshness as f; r=iter([10**12, 999*10**9, 9995*10**8, 9999*10**8, 99995*10**7]); s=SystemClock(wall_source=lambda: next(r), monotonic_source=lambda: 0); t=s.now_ns(); print([f.is_fresh(now_ns=s.now_ns(), reference_ns=t, max_age_ns=10**6) for _ in range(2)], [f.is_expired(now_ns=s.now_ns(), valid_until_ns=t+1) for _ in range(2)], s.regressions_observed)" -> [True, True] [False, False] 4: data stays 'fresh' against a 1 ms limit and an approval that expired 1 ns after the step never expires. The mitigation named in the docstring ("health monitoring can fail closed on an unstable clock") is not reachable through the contract: the Clock protocol has only mode / now_ns / monotonic_ns and ClockReading has no health field. In addition `regressions_observed` counts clamped readings, not "observed backward steps" as section 3.2 (l.119) says: readings [100,90,91,92,99,100,101,50,102] contain 2 backward steps and yield 5.
findings.proposed_change: While the wall clock is behind, keep time moving from the monotonic source: now = last_wall + (monotonic_now - monotonic_at_last_wall), never frozen and never decreasing; count a step once. Add `regressions_observed` (or a `healthy` flag) to the Clock protocol and to ClockReading (MINOR change) and state in 3.3 that no risk may be created while the run clock is unhealthy. Add a test that an expiry is reached during a simulated backward step.

findings.area: Tick contract / SHARED_CONTRACTS 6.1 + 6.3 / gie/core/ordering.py merge_ordered, G09, S01 acceptance
findings.title: The receive-time rule for imported history contradicts 'ordering time MUST be non-decreasing'; out-of-order historical ticks make the stream unmergeable
findings.detail:
gie/contracts/tick.py:66-71: receive_time_ns "For imported history without a recorded receive time ... equals event_time_ns plus the modelled feed delay." SHARED_CONTRACTS 6.1 (l.224): "Within a stream the ordering time MUST be non-decreasing" (ordering time of Tick = receive_time_ns). 6.3: "A quote whose source timestamp is older than its predecessor's keeps its arrival position and is flagged OUT_OF_ORDER; nothing is reordered". For imported history (the normal case: master G09 "raw ticks not stored in Round 2") an out-of-order source timestamp therefore produces a DECREASING ordering time at an increasing seq.
Reproducer: three fixture ticks with receive = event + 2 ms, events at T0, T0+10 ms, T0+4 ms (third flagged OUT_OF_ORDER): SequenceTracker accepts all three, but list(merge_ordered([(ordering_key(t), t) for t in ticks])) raises OutOfOrderError "input stream is not strictly ascending (seq=2, stream='tick/fixture/XAUUSD')" and sorted(ticks, key=ordering_key) yields seq order [0, 2, 1] - i.e. the EventKey order silently reorders what 6.3 forbids to reorder. Session 01's acceptance test "Out-of-order, duplicate, missing and stale tick tests; ... deterministic replay" cannot satisfy both rules, and 01 and 10 will resolve it differently. Nothing checks the per-stream time rule at ingest: SequenceTracker.observe takes no time, so the violation is only detected lazily at merge.
findings.proposed_change: Define the rule in 6.3 and in the Tick field doc: for imported history receive_time_ns = max(event_time_ns + modelled delay, receive_time_ns of the previous tick of the stream). Enforce it where it is cheap: let SequenceTracker.observe take the ordering time and refuse a decreasing one (new error or OutOfOrderError), and add a fixture test with an OUT_OF_ORDER historical tick that must merge.

findings.area: Identity / Evidence.market_event_id, gie/contracts/identity.py market_event_id, S02 acceptance 'exact event deduplication', G02
findings.title: market_event_id is neither verified nor recomputable, and its identity parts are unspecified - exact de-duplication rests on unchecked producer discipline
findings.detail: SHARED_CONTRACTS section 4: "market_event_id(kind, symbol, timeframe, anchor_time_ns, level_prices) is shared by every producer that observes the same event" and "Where all identity parts are fields of the record, the record verifies its own identifier on construction". kind, symbol, timeframe, anchor_time_ns and levels ARE fields of Evidence, but only EVD-1 exists (gie/contracts/evidence.py:207-212, evidence_id from engine/market_event_id/revision). Reproducers: S.evidence(market_event_id='mev_'+'0'*32) constructs; adding one descriptive level (PriceLevel WICK_LOW) to the same sweep changes the id (the fixture hashes ALL level prices, tests/gie/samples.py:165-175); an anchor 1 ns apart changes the id. Neither SHARED_CONTRACTS nor FIELDS.md says which level roles belong to the identity or which instant is the anchor of a sweep / FVG / breakout (candle open, candle close, the sweeping tick?). identity.market_event_id (identity.py:29-44) also validates nothing: prices passed as str ['2648.40'] or int are accepted and give a different id than Decimal('2648.40'); timeframe 'm5' vs 'M5' and a free-text kind are accepted. Two engines reporting the same sweep will therefore almost never collide, silently, and "Two Evidence records with equal market_event_id ... MUST be counted once" has no effect; brief 02 requires "Deduplicate shared sweep/FVG/breakout evidence" with acceptance "exact event deduplication".
findings.proposed_change: (1) Make the identity checkable now, independent of the engine audit: mark which levels are identity-defining (e.g. a boolean on PriceLevel or a normative per-kind list of identity roles) and add EVD-11: market_event_id == identity.market_event_id(kind, symbol, timeframe.value, anchor_time_ns, identity level prices). (2) Make identity functions validate their inputs (Decimal-only prices, Timeframe value, CODE_PATTERN kind, SYMBOL_PATTERN symbol, non-bool ints) and raise ContractValidationError. (3) Record as an explicit provisional item in section 11 that the anchor definition and identity roles of the three shared kinds must be fixed by session 02 before de-duplication can be claimed.

findings.area: Identity / candidate_id, alternative_group_id (CND-1, PLN-2), G01 hybrid horizon, G07 shadow validation
findings.title: candidate_id omits horizon and model version: distinct candidates collide and are forced into one mutually exclusive plan group
findings.detail: gie/contracts/identity.py:51-52: candidate_id = make_id('cnd', setup_type, side, sorted(set(evidence_ids)), revision). Horizon, model_version_id, producer and run are not part of it. Master G01 requires "hybrid scalping and intraday"; G07 requires "shadow validation" (brief 09: "shadow compare"), i.e. the same evidence scored by an active and a shadow model. Reproducer: python3 -B -c "from tests.gie import samples as S; from gie.contracts import Horizon, identity as i; a=S.candidate(); b=S.candidate(horizon=Horizon.INTRADAY, expected_net_r=0.9); print(a.candidate_id==b.candidate_id, a==b, i.alternative_group_id(a.candidate_id)==i.alternative_group_id(b.candidate_id))" -> True False True. Two different records share one id (TradePlan.candidate_id becomes ambiguous for 05/09/11), and because alternative_group_id derives from candidate_id (PLN-2) and the TradePlan docstring says plans sharing it are "mutually exclusive ... at most one of them may ever be executed", the scalp and the intraday opportunity - or the active and the shadow scoring - are forced into one exclusive group. The uniqueness scope of every identifier (global vs per run) is also not stated in section 4: evd/cnd/pln ids repeat across runs with different content while rsk/ord/pos ids include the run.
findings.proposed_change: Decide and document the identity: include horizon and the scoring model (model_version_id, or null for unscored) in candidate_id - or state normatively that setup_type must encode them - and add a table to section 4 giving, per prefix, the identity parts and the uniqueness scope (global / per run). Add a test that two candidates differing only in horizon or model version cannot share an id.

findings.area: S00-ASG-23 freshness / SHARED_CONTRACTS 3.1 + 3.3, gie/core/freshness.py, G03
findings.title: The freshness reference instant and the meaning of as_of_time_ns are not defined per contract
findings.detail: The coordinator brief requires Session 00 to "Define units, timestamps, IDs, freshness". Section 3.3 only says "Data with a reference instant is fresh iff 0 <= now_ns - reference_ns < max_age_ns" without naming the reference field of any contract. For Tick there are two candidates. Using event_time_ns is natural for 'stale quote' but TICK-2 explicitly allows event_time_ns > receive_time_ns (flag EVENT_AFTER_RECEIVE, broker clock ahead), and then the helper raises in replay where the tolerance MUST be 0: f.require_fresh(now_ns=T0, reference_ns=T0+5, max_age_ns=10**9, what='tick') -> FutureDataError. One session will use receive time, another event time. The rule "A tolerance ... MUST be 0 in replay" (l.133) is not enforceable by the helpers, which take plain ints and never see the clock mode. as_of_time_ns is "the receive time of the newest input it depends on" (3.1): for a RiskDecision or Position derived from other GIE records plus account state it is undefined whether that is the newest transitive market input or the newest direct input, and "End-to-end delay of a decision is decision_time_ns - as_of_time_ns" (l.101) then measures the time since the NEWEST input - a plan built on five-minute-old evidence but risk-checked against the latest tick reports a near-zero delay. Master G03 asks to "measure p50/p95/p99/max and end-to-end delays, reject stale signals"; brief 02 tests "no five-minute notification delay".
findings.proposed_change: Add a normative table to 3.3: per contract the reference instant for age (Tick: receive_time_ns; quote staleness = receive_time_ns - event_time_ns, which is what TickFlag.STALE means; feed silence = now - receive time of the last tick), and for derived records whether age is taken from as_of_time_ns or only valid_until_ns applies. Define as_of_time_ns as the maximum receive time over all transitive market inputs, and if end-to-end delay is to be reported from a record add the triggering input's receive time (e.g. trigger_time_ns) or define the delay as a join over the id chain. Add a helper that takes the Clock and refuses a non-zero tolerance when clock.mode is REPLAY.

findings.area: S00-ACC-02 compatibility / gie/contracts/compat.py, schema_gen.py, SHARED_CONTRACTS section 8
findings.title: State machines, transition validators, identity functions, canonical-order keys and invariant code are outside the schema lock: a breaking change needs no version bump
findings.detail: Section 8 promises that CI fails "if the difference to an earlier version of the same MAJOR is larger than the declared bump" and classifies a changed "invariant" as MAJOR. compat.py compares JSON Schemas only, and the schemas carry of the behaviour just the invariant id + rule TEXT (x-gie-invariants), a boolean x-gie-unique and a label x-gie-canonical-order. Not locked at all: ORDER_TRANSITIONS and validate_order_transition, MODEL_STATUS_TRANSITIONS (the safety rule "A model can be ACTIVE only after SHADOW", section 9), validate_position_transition, every identity function, the canonical sort key functions, the invariant lambdas, StreamRank, stream names and error codes. Reproducer (in-memory only): import gie.contracts.order_event as oe, gie.contracts.model_version as mv, gie.contracts.identity as idn; oe.ORDER_TRANSITIONS.clear(); mv.MODEL_STATUS_TRANSITIONS[mv.ModelStatus.RESEARCH] = frozenset(mv.ModelStatus); idn.plan_id = lambda *a: 'pln_' + '0'*32; from gie.contracts import schema_gen; print(schema_gen.check()) -> [] (no problem reported). FIELDS.md is regenerated, and `render_contract_docs --check` only checks that it is current, not that a version was bumped. The only backstop named in section 8, golden messages under tests/gie/golden/, did not exist at 9784ea6 (acceptance_tests.yaml l.22-24 lists tests/gie/contracts/test_roundtrip.py and test_golden.py, neither present), and golden single messages would not cover lifecycle rules anyway.
findings.proposed_change: Put the behavioural surface under the same lock: emit the transition tables, immutable/replaceable field lists, per-prefix identity part lists, stream-name templates and rank into the generated schemas as x-gie-* keywords (then compat.py already classifies any change as MAJOR), or add a 'semantic lock' hash of a generated canonical description to LOCK.json per contract version. Add golden lifecycle traces (order, position, model) that must stay valid, and commit the golden messages before the gate.

findings.area: Clock contract / gie/core/clock.py PollingScheduler (UNCOMMITTED working tree at 10:50 UTC, lines 284-335)
findings.title: PollingScheduler is not replay-equivalent: call_at(now) raises in paper, and run_due fires timers that are due after the pending input
findings.detail: The new module docstring states that timers make "paper and replay equivalent" and that "a timer due at instant t fires before any input that became available at t is delivered". (a) call_at raises ClockRegressionError when due_ns < clock.now_ns() (l.305-308). In replay virtual time is frozen, so call_at(clock.now_ns(), cb) or call_at(tick.receive_time_ns, cb) is legal; in paper the wall clock has moved between the read and the call, so the identical code raises. Reproducer: seq=iter([100,105,105,110]); sc=SystemClock(wall_source=lambda: next(seq), monotonic_source=lambda: 0); PollingScheduler(sc).call_at(sc.now_ns(), lambda t: None) -> ClockRegressionError "timer scheduled in the past (due_ns=100, now_ns=105)", while ReplayClock(100).call_at(100, cb) returns handle 0. (b) run_due() pops every timer due at or before the CURRENT clock reading (l.328), not at or before the availability time of the input that is about to be delivered. Input stamped receive_time 100, timer due 110, poll at 120: paper order is timer@110 then input@100; replaying the recorded input with ReplayClock gives input@100 then timer@110. A recorded paper session therefore does not replay to the same record sequence (section 6.2 l.239-241). This code was uncommitted while I reviewed and may still change; SHARED_CONTRACTS 3.2 does not yet describe Scheduler at all.
findings.proposed_change: (a) In paper a due time at or before now must not be an error: fire it at the next poll ("never early" still holds); if the error is kept for replay, document the asymmetry and give components a single safe idiom. (b) Give run_due a limit: run_due(limit_ns = receive time of the next input) before delivering that input, and plain now only when idle. Add a test that records inputs under SystemClock + PollingScheduler and asserts the same callback/record order when replayed through ReplayClock, and add Scheduler to section 3.2 and the Clock contract description.

findings.area: Units / exact decimals: gie/contracts/trade_plan.py:261, gie/contracts/order_event.py:407, SHARED_CONTRACTS section 2
findings.title: Two decimal operations use the ambient decimal context instead of EXACT
findings.detail: Section 2 (l.72-74): "Arithmetic on these exact decimals MUST use the context gie.core.canonical.EXACT ... Python's default decimal context rounds silently at 28 digits and MUST NOT be used for them." (1) TradePlan.risk_per_unit returns abs(EXACT.subtract(...)); Decimal.__abs__ rounds to the current thread context. Reproducer: plan with entry 123456789012345678.123456789012 and stop 0.000000000001 -> risk_per_unit 123456789012345678.1234567890, exact value ...123456789011; with realistic prices but an ambient context of prec=4 (decimal.localcontext set by any library or notebook): entry 2649.80, stop 2637.455 -> risk_per_unit 12.34 instead of 12.345. (2) validate_order_transition computes previous.cumulative_filled_lots + event.last_fill_lots with the `+` operator. Under an ambient prec=3 context: volume 12.34, fills 10.01 then 1.04 - the WRONG cumulative 11.0 is accepted and the correct 11.05 is refused; with 30-digit wire values even the default context refuses a correct first fill (0 + 100000000000000000.000000000001). Realistic gold values are safe under the default context, but the result depends on global mutable state, which is exactly what the rule forbids.
findings.proposed_change: Use EXACT.abs(...) (or .copy_abs()) in risk_per_unit and EXACT.add(...) in validate_order_transition. Add a CI check (AST scan of gie/contracts and later subsystem packages) that forbids arithmetic operators and abs()/sum() on contract decimals outside EXACT, and one test that runs the validators under decimal.localcontext(prec=3).

findings.area: Identity / SHARED_CONTRACTS section 4 'Recomputable', Position, Evidence/Candidate/TradePlan revision links, OrderEvent.client_order_id
findings.title: Identifiers whose parts are all on the record are not verified; client_order_id cannot be recomputed from an OrderEvent
findings.detail: Section 4 (l.165-167): "Where all identity parts are fields of the record, the record verifies its own identifier on construction (EVD-1, CND-1, PLN-1, PLN-2, RSK-1, RSK-3, OEV-1, MDL-1)." Not covered although verifiable: (a) Position.position_id of a GIE-owned position = identity.position_id(run_id, opening_client_order_id), both fields of the record (gie/contracts/position.py has POS-1..7, none on the id): S.position(position_id='pos_'+'0'*32) constructs. (b) supersedes_evidence_id / supersedes_candidate_id / supersedes_plan_id are only checked for presence (EVD-7, CND-7, PLN-10): S.evidence(revision=1, supersedes_evidence_id='evd_'+'f'*32) constructs although the predecessor id is computable from the same fields with revision-1. (c) identity.client_order_id(run, origin_id, intent, attempt) (identity.py:72-79): `attempt` is not a field of OrderEvent, so the idempotency key of G08 ("idempotent orders") cannot be re-derived or audited from the journal except by brute force over attempt numbers; the meaning of attempt for several simultaneous orders of the same intent on one position (up to 8 targets) is also undefined.
findings.proposed_change: Add POS-8 (GIE owner: position_id == identity.position_id(run_id, opening_client_order_id)); add checks that supersedes_* equals the id of revision-1 where the other identity parts are unchanged (or document when they may change); add `attempt` (and, if several orders of one intent may coexist, a slot/leg index) to OrderEvent and verify client_order_id. All are possible in place while the lock is PROPOSED.

findings.area: Serialisation / gie/contracts/codec.py:63-65 fingerprint, SHARED_CONTRACTS 6.1 + 8
findings.title: The fingerprint covers the envelope schema_version, so a documentation-only PATCH bump turns an identical record into a SequenceConflict
findings.detail: fingerprint(value) = content_hash(to_wire(value)) includes "schema_version". Section 8: "PATCH never affects decoding" and PATCH is "documentation only"; section 6.1: "same position and identical content - an idempotent duplicate that is dropped; same position and different content - SequenceConflictError"; RecordSink.publish "must be idempotent per (stream, seq)". Reproducer: w=codec.to_wire(S.tick()); w2=dict(w, schema_version='1.0.1'); codec.from_wire(w2)==S.tick() -> True, but content_hash(w)==content_hash(w2) -> False, and SequenceTracker().observe(stream, 0, hash(w)) followed by observe(stream, 0, hash(w2)) raises SequenceConflictError. After any contract version bump - even a description fix - re-publishing or re-deriving a journaled record during restart reconciliation (G08) is reported as a conflict, and byte-for-byte replay comparisons across the bump fail for every record.
findings.proposed_change: Either compute the duplicate-detection fingerprint over contract name + MAJOR + fields (excluding MINOR/PATCH), or state normatively in section 8 that journals and replay comparisons are only valid at identical contract versions and that a bump requires a journal cut-over; add the PATCH case to the compatibility tests.

findings.area: Validation / gie/contracts/_spec.py Float.check (l.285-302) vs Float.decode (l.307-316), SHARED_CONTRACTS 5.2
findings.title: Float fields silently round integers on construction although the decoder refuses the same value
findings.detail: Section 5.2: invalid input "is never clamped, defaulted, rounded or coerced". Float.check converts with float(value) and keeps the result; Float.decode explicitly refuses an integer that is "not exactly representable as a double". Reproducer: python3 -B -c "from gie.contracts import NamedValue; print(NamedValue(name='x1', value=2**53+1).value)" -> 9007199254740992.0 (off by one, no error), while the same value in a wire message is rejected by from_wire. A producer that passes an integer count or id as a feature/metric gets a silently different number in the record, its fingerprint and the journal.
findings.proposed_change: In Float.check apply the decode rule (refuse an int whose float() does not compare equal to it), or refuse ints altogether and require producers to pass floats; add the case to the round-trip tests.

findings.area: Error semantics / gie/contracts/registry.py:27-33 parse_semver, gie/contracts/codec.py:88
findings.title: A very long schema_version makes from_wire raise ValueError instead of a GieError
findings.detail: Section 5: "All errors derive from gie.core.errors.GieError". _SEMVER_RE allows components of unbounded length and parse_semver converts them with int(); beyond CPython's 4300-digit limit this raises ValueError. Reproducer: w=codec.to_wire(S.tick()); w['schema_version']='1.0.'+'9'*5000; codec.from_wire(w) -> ValueError "Exceeds the limit (4300 digits) for integer string conversion" (same through from_json). A consumer that handles GieError to fail closed and journal the error crashes on this input instead. strict_loads already guards integer literals (MAX_INTEGER_LITERAL_CHARS); the version string is the remaining path.
findings.proposed_change: Bound the components in the pattern, e.g. (0|[1-9][0-9]{0,8}) for each part (SEMVER_PATTERN is also published in the schemas, so do it while the lock is PROPOSED), or catch ValueError in parse_semver and raise ContractVersionError.

findings.area: Schemas / gie/contracts/_spec.py schema() methods vs decode paths, gie/contracts/schemas/*.json
findings.title: Structural rules where the published JSON Schema and the Python decoder disagree
findings.detail: Verified with jsonschema Draft 2020-12 against the generated schemas: (1) Int fields are published as {"type":"integer"}, which by JSON Schema accepts 5.0 / 5e0; Int.decode (_spec.py:181-184) rejects any float token: Tick with "seq": 5.0 -> schema valid, decoder "seq: must be a JSON integer". (2) Float fields are {"type":"number"}: the schema accepts 9007199254740993 and non-canonical integers beyond 64 bits, the decoder rejects both. (3) Pattern-less strings (Position.external_ref, ModelVersion.approved_by): the schema accepts control characters such as TAB, Str.check rejects them via isprintable() (l.110-111) - a rule that also varies with the Unicode version of the Python runtime. (4) Uniqueness is published only as the private keyword x-gie-unique although the standard uniqueItems would enforce it for the scalar lists (flags, reason codes, evidence_ids): duplicate flags are schema valid and decoder invalid. (5) TRADING_DAY_PATTERN accepts 2026-02-30. (6) Validator dependence: python-jsonschema evaluates patterns with Python `re`, where `$` matches before a trailing newline, so it accepts "bid": "2650.10\n" while the decoder (after 9784ea6) and any ECMA-262 validator reject it - a schema-versus-decoder agreement test written with python-jsonschema will report a false difference. In all cases the schema is the laxer side (no fail-open in the decoder), but session 11 and any non-Python tool will treat schema-valid messages as decodable.
findings.proposed_change: State in SHARED_CONTRACTS section 7 and in each schema ($comment) that the schema is necessary but not sufficient and list the decoder-only rules; add uniqueItems: true to the scalar lists; publish the integer-token rule (integers must be written without fraction or exponent); for free-text strings either publish a pattern that excludes control characters or define the allowed character set explicitly instead of str.isprintable().

findings.area: Serialisation / SHARED_CONTRACTS section 7 vs gie/core/canonical.py _parse_int (l.252-275) after commit 9784ea6
findings.title: The prose wire rules were not updated for the new 'large integer literal is a double' rule, and the module docstring disagrees with the code
findings.detail: Section 7 still says "Parsing is strict: ... no integers beyond 64 bits" (l.269) and "Readers MUST parse JSON integers exactly as 64-bit integers; ... JavaScript consumers need a BigInt-aware parser" (l.258-260). Since 9784ea6 strict_loads accepts an integer literal beyond 64 bits when it is the canonical rendering of a double: strict_loads('10000000000000000000') -> 1e+19 (float), while '9223372036854775808' is refused. That fix is sound, but it is a wire rule that every non-Python reader (dashboard, session 11; QA tools) must know: a float field may arrive as an integer literal of up to 21 digits, and a float such as 1.0 arrives as `1`, so a BigInt-aware parser yields BigInt for float fields unless it consults the field type. The rule exists only in the canonical.py docstring, which itself says a larger literal is accepted if it "is exactly a double" (l.21-25) whereas the code requires the canonical ES rendering (l.270) - 18446744073709555712 (2^64+4096, exactly a double) is refused.
findings.proposed_change: Update section 7: (a) number tokens do not carry their type, the contract field type decides; (b) float fields may be written as integer literals, up to 21 digits, and readers must accept exactly the canonical rendering; (c) correct the docstring. Add golden messages containing a float field with value 1.0 and one with 1e19 so that every reader implementation is tested on both.

findings.area: Serialisation / canonical order: Evidence.levels, Candidate.destinations, TradePlan.targets
findings.title: Three lists have neither a canonical order nor uniqueness nor a documented order meaning
findings.detail: Section 7 (l.266-268): "Lists whose order carries no meaning have a defined canonical order (x-gie-canonical-order in the schema)". Evidence.levels (gie/contracts/evidence.py:174-176, "Price levels that describe the event"), Candidate.destinations (candidate.py:149-151, "Scenario price destinations") and TradePlan.targets (trade_plan.py:148-150, "Profit destinations, at least one") are plain ListOf(Obj(...)) without canonical_sort or unique_key, and FIELDS.md does not say that their order is meaningful; duplicates (two levels with the same role and price, two targets at the same price) are accepted. Two producers - or one producer iterating a set, whose order depends on PYTHONHASHSEED - emit the same content with different bytes and fingerprints, which breaks the byte-for-byte replay requirement (l.239-241) and idempotent duplicate detection for reasons that no test of the producer logic will reveal.
findings.proposed_change: Give levels a canonical order (role, price) with uniqueness on (role, price); destinations a canonical order and uniqueness by label; for targets either document that the order is meaningful (and add an invariant, e.g. ordered by distance from the entry, no duplicate price) or sort canonically by price distance. All are in-place corrections while the lock is PROPOSED.

findings.area: Ordering / gie/core/ordering.py SequenceTracker (l.125-205), SHARED_CONTRACTS 6.1
findings.title: SequenceTracker: stream start, restart and input checks are weaker than section 6.1 states
findings.detail: (1) Section 6.1: every stream numbers its records "starting at 0"; with the default first_seq=None the first arrival is accepted at any seq (SequenceTracker().observe('s', 7, 'h') -> ACCEPTED), so a stream that lost its head is not noticed. (2) first_seq is one value for all streams of a tracker, so resuming several streams after a restart (G08 "restart reconciliation") needs one tracker per stream, and a re-sent record from before the restart is classified as a gap: SequenceTracker(first_seq=6).observe('s', 5, 'g') -> SequenceGapError "stream does not start at the required first sequence number" although it is an old duplicate. There is no way to seed last seq + recent fingerprints from a journal other than replaying observe(). (3) The fingerprint is not validated: observe('s', 0, None) twice -> the duplicate is reported as OutOfOrderError because a stored None is read as 'not kept' (l.184-185). (4) window and first_seq are not type/range checked (window=True, first_seq=-1 accepted). (5) The per-stream rule "the ordering time MUST be non-decreasing" cannot be checked because observe() takes no time (see the imported-history finding).
findings.proposed_change: Require a non-empty str fingerprint; validate window/first_seq; add a restore(stream, last_seq, recent) (or per-stream first_seq) so a restarted consumer can continue and classify pre-restart re-sends as DUPLICATE or OutOfOrderError; make first_seq=0 the documented default for run-scoped streams; optionally accept the ordering time in observe().

findings.area: Versioning / gie/contracts/registry.py:45-52, gie/contracts/codec.py:89-95, tools/make_golden.py:59-64, SHARED_CONTRACTS section 8
findings.title: There is no read path across MAJOR versions, and the golden check as written will fail after the first MAJOR bump
findings.detail: The registry holds exactly one class per contract name ("contract ... is already registered", registry.py:48) and from_wire refuses any other MAJOR (codec.py:89-95). After the first MAJOR bump every journal and every golden message of the previous MAJOR is undecodable by the current code. Section 8 says golden messages "must decode forever within their MAJOR", but tools/make_golden.py check() decodes EVERY file under tests/gie/golden/*/ with the current code (l.59-64: `for path in sorted(root.glob('*/*.json')) ... from_json(text)`), so the old-MAJOR directories will raise ContractVersionError and the check can only pass by deleting them. Master G07 ("Historical replay and market memory") and G08 ("Persistent state") imply reading records written earlier in the project.
findings.proposed_change: Decide before the first MAJOR bump: either key the registry by (name, MAJOR) so that old readers stay available, or require a migration tool per MAJOR bump and say so in section 8. In make_golden.check() skip (and list) directories of other MAJORs, or decode them with the reader of their MAJOR.

findings.area: Identity / ordering scope: SHARED_CONTRACTS 4 + 6.1, Tick, stream names in gie/contracts/ordering.py:27-40, RecordSink
findings.title: The scope of a stream's seq is undefined; ticks have no run or dataset scope and stream names carry no run
findings.detail: Section 4 (l.176): "A stream position is (stream name, seq); a tick is identified by (source, symbol, seq)"; section 6.1: seq starts "at 0". Tick has no run_id (gie/contracts/tick.py) and stream names are `<contract>/<producer>` or `tick/<source>/<symbol>` without a run. It is not stated when a stream begins: per run, per process start, per imported dataset, or once for ever. Consequences: a restarted paper feed handler or a second import of the same history re-issues (source, symbol, 0..n) for different quotes; two runs publishing into one RecordSink (whose contract is "idempotent per (stream, seq)", gie/contracts/interfaces.py) collide at evidence/<producer> seq 0 with a SequenceConflictError; and a replay of a sub-range has no rule whether tick seq starts at 0 or at the position in the dataset. Brief 01 asks for "sequence IDs" and deterministic replay, so 01 and 10 need the same answer.
findings.proposed_change: Define the scope normatively: for run-scoped records the stream key is (run_id, stream) and seq continues across restarts of the same run from the journal; for ticks either add a dataset / ingest-session identifier to Tick or state that tick seq is assigned once at ingest into the tick store and never restarts, and that replay preserves the stored seq.

findings.area: Small inconsistencies in gie/core and gie/contracts/_spec.py (time, parsing, documentation)
findings.title: Remaining edge cases and doc/code mismatches
findings.detail: (1) gie/core/timeutil.py: trading_day_bounds_ns is not total over the range of trading_day(): trading_day(0) == '1970-01-01' but trading_day_bounds_ns('1970-01-01') now raises "datetime outside the supported instant range" (Prague midnight is 1969-12-31T23:00Z); likewise trading_day(MAX_TIME_NS) == '2262-04-12' has no bounds. (2) gie/core/canonical.py strict_loads('1e-400') returns 0.0: a non-zero wire number silently becomes zero (overflow is refused, underflow is not), against "never ... rounded" (section 5.2). (3) ReplayClock docstring: "advancing to the current instant is a no-op", but advance_to(now) fires timers due now (c=ReplayClock(100); c.call_at(100, cb); c.advance_to(100) calls cb). (4) _spec.py ListOf docstring says canonical_sort is "a key function over encoded items" (l.423-425) while it is applied to in-memory items (l.458-459). (5) Errors raised inside nested records carry a relative path: a bad level price reports "price: must be > 0" with path='price' and only parent_path='levels[0]' (decode_fields l.663-670), although section 5.2 promises an error "naming the field path". (6) gie/core/freshness.py: the tolerance rule of 3.3 and the int checks accept negative now_ns / reference_ns (is_fresh(now_ns=-5, reference_ns=-6, max_age_ns=10) -> True) although instants are defined as 0 .. 2^63-1.
findings.proposed_change: (1) Clamp the bounds to [0, MAX_TIME_NS] or document the two unsupported days. (2) Refuse a literal that parses to 0.0 but is not written as zero. (3)-(4) Correct the docstrings. (5) Join parent path and field path into details['path'] and the message. (6) Use the instant range check of timeutil for now_ns / reference_ns / valid_until_ns.

findings.area: CR-003 / additional shared contracts, gie/core/ordering.py StreamRank, gie/contracts/ordering.py ordering_key, G03
findings.title: From the time/ordering lens a shared Candle contract is REQUIRED before sessions 02, 03 and 10 consume candles
findings.detail: Master G03: "strategic on completed candles"; brief 01: "candle construction"; brief 02 adapts six engines that work on candles. The look-ahead-critical definitions of a candle are time definitions: open instant, close instant and above all the AVAILABILITY instant (the receive time of the tick or the timer that completes it), plus its place in the total order. Today StreamRank has no candle rank, ordering_key raises UnknownContractError for any record outside the nine contracts, and the stream table of section 6.1 has no row for it; if 01 and 02 each define these locally, prefix invariance (S02) and no-look-ahead (S10) cannot be tested across sessions. CR-003 / U-11 already record that Candle, InstrumentSpec and AccountSnapshot are expected; this note only states explicitly that, in my judgement, Candle is REQUIRED (not optional) before 02/03 start and before 10 builds the replay driver, and that adding it touches gie.core.ordering (rank, stream name, ordering time), not only gie.contracts. This goes beyond the nine contracts named in the Session 00 brief, hence severity note.
findings.proposed_change: Make the Candle proposal the first deliverable of session 01 and require it to specify: open/close instants, availability time (= ordering time), rank relative to TICK and ORDER_EVENT, stream name, the rule for an empty or quiet interval (closed by timer), and its trading-day / DST behaviour. Add an extension rule to section 6.1 for how a new contract obtains a rank and an ordering time.

findings.area: Determinism / SHARED_CONTRACTS 3.2 + 6.2, gie/core/clock.py, gie/core/latency.py, G03, G10
findings.title: Deterministic replay of asynchronous background updates and of decision latency is not specified
findings.detail: Master G03 allows "asynchronous background updates" for the strategic layer and asks to "measure ... end-to-end delays, reject stale signals"; G10 asks for "cost/latency stress"; section 6.2 demands byte-for-byte identical replays. In replay virtual time does not advance while code runs (section 3.2), so every age is 0 and every decision_time_ns equals the triggering receive time: staleness-driven rejections can never occur in replay, and measured latencies (time.perf_counter_ns via LatencyRecorder) are real-time values that must never enter a record. Nothing states how a background result (model refresh, slow strategic computation) enters the replay timeline deterministically, or how modelled compute/feed latency is charged. This is beyond what the specification states for Session 00, hence severity note, but sessions 04, 05, 06 and 10 will otherwise each invent a different rule, and the uncommitted Scheduler work (clock.py) is the natural place to fix it.
findings.proposed_change: Add to section 3.2 / 6.2: background results are delivered as records at a virtual availability instant scheduled through the injected Scheduler (call_at with a modelled, seeded delay), never when a thread happens to finish; modelled decision latency is applied the same way; LatencyRecorder output is evidence only and must not appear in contract records or influence decisions in replay.
